special:1.en: Ali handed me a small device with no markings. 'It has a *special* frequency,' she said quietly. 'Zero's team cannot detect it.' I clipped it to my collar and stepped into the open street. The rain had stopped. That felt wrong — the silence was too clean, too still.
special:1.cnHint: 阿栗给了我一个有____频率的装置，但我走上街头时，那片异常的寂静让我不安。
special:1.hook: In Harbor City, silence was never a good sign.
special:1.line: 'This has a *special* frequency — Zero cannot hear it,' Ali said.

text:1.en: A small screen on the wall flickered to life as I passed. One line of *text* appeared, white on black: THEY KNOW YOU ARE HERE. Then it went dark. I kept walking, steady pace, eyes forward. If I ran, I was finished. If I stopped, same result.
text:1.cnHint: 墙上的屏幕突然亮起，一行____出现后立刻熄灭，内容让我心跳加速。
text:1.hook: My next step could be my last free one.
text:1.line: 'Read that *text* again — every word is a warning,' Grey Crow said.

front:1.en: I came around the corner and stopped. Zero was standing at the *front* of the old signal tower, back straight, hood down, facing me directly. No guards. No cover. Just the two of us on a wet empty street under a sky full of dead satellites.
front:1.cnHint: 转过街角，我看见零点就站在旧信号塔的____，直视着我。
front:1.hook: Zero smiled, and that was the most frightening thing yet.
front:1.line: 'Meet me at the *front* of the tower — come alone,' Zero had said.

law:1.en: Grey Crow spread his hands. 'You cannot use the *law* against Zero here — the city council is bought, the judges are blind, the records are forged.' I stared at the wet pavement. Then I looked up. There was one channel left that Zero had not yet closed.
law:1.cnHint: 灰鸦告诉我，在这座城市里____已经失效，对付零点只剩最后一条路。
law:1.hook: That last channel was the most dangerous one of all.
law:1.line: 'The *law* won't touch Zero — we have to find another way,' Grey Crow said.

himself:0.en: The signal room was silent except for the hum of old machines. Grey Crow stood at the center console, checking every wire *himself*. He trusted no one else with this. One wrong connection and the whole broadcast would collapse — and with it, our only chance to expose Zero.
himself:0.cnHint: 灰鸦亲自在信号室检查每一根线路，因为这次任务容不得任何差错。
himself:0.hook: Then one wire glowed red — and it was not supposed to.
himself:0.line: 'I do this *himself* — no one touches these wires but me.'

landscape:0.en: Ali pulled up the city map on the cracked screen. The data *landscape* spread before us like a glowing grid — every encrypted node, every dead signal, every hidden route Zero had used. It was beautiful and terrifying at once. Somewhere in that web was the answer.
landscape:0.cnHint: 阿栗展开了城市的数据____，我们试图从中找到零点的藏身之处。
landscape:0.hook: One node pulsed twice, then went dark forever.
landscape:0.line: 'Look at this *landscape* — Zero left his marks everywhere.'

mentally:0.en: I sat in the corner of the safe room, eyes closed. Grey Crow said to rest, but I was *mentally* mapping every move Zero had made in the last three days. Each step, each signal, each silence. When I opened my eyes, I knew which door he would use.
mentally:0.cnHint: 调查员在休息室里____推演零点的每一步行动，试图预判他的下一个目标。
mentally:0.hook: The door at the end of the hall clicked open.
mentally:0.line: 'I am *mentally* three steps ahead of him already.'

neither:0.en: Grey Crow laid two data chips on the table. *Neither* one held the full code — Zero had split it on purpose. Without both chips active at the same time, the locked broadcast would stay dark. Ali and I looked at each other. We had only one chip.
neither:0.cnHint: 桌上的两块芯片____单独包含完整密码，零点显然早有安排。
neither:0.hook: Ali's hand moved to her coat pocket and stopped cold.
neither:0.line: '*Neither* chip works alone — he planned this from the start.'

onto:0.en: Ali threw the decryption key *onto* the console screen and it landed in the active slot with a sharp click. The room filled with static, then a voice — cold and flat — began to read coordinates. Grey Crow grabbed his earpiece. This was the signal we had waited days to hear.
onto:0.cnHint: 阿栗将解密密钥投____控制台，隐藏的信号终于开始播报坐标。
onto:0.hook: The coordinates pointed to a place we had already burned.
onto:0.line: 'Drop it *onto* the slot — now, before the window closes.'

plus:0.en: Grey Crow wrote the equation on the fogged glass: signal strength *plus* location data equals Zero's next broadcast point. It was simple math, but no one had tried it before. Ali ran the numbers twice. The result was a single address in the lower port district.
plus:0.cnHint: 灰鸦用一个简单公式——信号强度____位置数据——锁定了零点的下一个广播地点。
plus:0.hook: The address matched a building we thought was empty.
plus:0.line: 'Frequency *plus* position — that is how we find him tonight.'

root:0.en: I found the line of corrupted code at last. It was buried deep, but this was the *root* of every false signal Zero had sent us over the past week. Pull this one thread and his whole network would unravel. Grey Crow leaned over my shoulder and said nothing for a long moment.
root:0.cnHint: 调查员终于找到了零点虚假信号的____，只要切断它，整个网络就会崩溃。
root:0.hook: Grey Crow finally spoke: 'Don't touch it yet.'
root:0.line: 'This is the *root* — cut it and his whole web falls.'

satisfy:0.en: Zero's message was short: meet at the old relay station or he would erase every piece of evidence we had collected. It did not *satisfy* Grey Crow. He read it three times, jaw tight, then set it down. 'It is a trap,' he said. 'But we have no other road.'
satisfy:0.cnHint: 零点的条件根本无法____灰鸦，但我们似乎已经别无选择。
satisfy:0.hook: Ali was already checking her gear by the back door.
satisfy:0.line: 'This deal does not *satisfy* me — but we move anyway.'

earth:1.en: Zero's broadcast cut through every channel at once: 'There is no safe ground left in Harbor City. The *earth* under your feet is already ours.' I stood at the edge of the district square, rain soaking through my jacket, and felt the cracked pavement shift — just slightly — beneath me. A tremor. Or a signal.
earth:1.cnHint: 零点的广播让我意识到，脚下的____已不再安全，整个城市正处于他们的掌控之中。
earth:1.hook: The pavement cracked open in a neat, deliberate line.
earth:1.line: 'They planted sensors in the *earth* along every route you know.'

paper:1.en: A thin sheet of *paper* was pinned to the lamp post at the corner of Dock Nine — an almost forgotten thing in a city of screens. The words were handwritten in pale ink: a meeting point, a time, a warning. Ali had left it. I pulled it free, read it twice, then held it over a heat vent until it was gone.
paper:1.cnHint: 阿栗在路灯柱上留下了一张____，上面手写着碰面地点和一个警告。
paper:1.hook: The ink, I realized too late, had already transferred to my fingers.
paper:1.line: 'The *paper* looks blank — but heat will show you what Ali wrote.'

art:1.en: The coded graffiti covering the sub-station wall was not random noise. Grey Crow had called it *art* — a living cipher that rewrote itself each night. I scanned each layer, peeling the visual signals apart in my mind. The outermost marks were decoys. The real message sat underneath, painted in a frequency only I could read.
art:1.cnHint: 格雷·克罗告诉我，变电站墙上的加密涂鸦是一种____，每晚都会自我改写，表层只是伪装。
art:1.hook: The innermost layer spelled out my own case number.
art:1.line: 'Zero turned code into *art* — that is what makes him so hard to catch.'

street:1.en: Every *street* in the harbor district had a sound — a low hum coded into the traffic signals. I had learned to tell them apart. Tonight the hum on Canal Row was wrong, half a tone too high. Someone had rewritten the signal grid. I walked slower, scanning doorways, roof edges, the dark space between parked transport pods.
street:1.cnHint: 港区每条____都有独特的编码信号音，今晚运河街的信号音被篡改了，有人动了手脚。
street:1.hook: At the far end of the block, a figure stepped into the light and stopped.
street:1.line: 'Clear the *street* — this whole grid is a trap set for you.'

talent:1.en: Grey Crow looked me over in the grey pre-dawn light, rain still falling. 'Your *talent* is rare,' they said, quiet and flat. 'Most people hear noise. You hear structure.' I did not answer. Somewhere below, Zero's network was already shifting, erasing tracks, building new walls of code. Rare was not the same as ready.
talent:1.cnHint: 格雷·克罗评价我有罕见的____——别人只听到噪音，而我能听出其中的结构。
talent:1.hook: 'But talent without speed,' Grey Crow added, 'is just a slow way to lose.'
talent:1.line: 'Raw *talent* means nothing if Zero finishes the upload first.'

overall:1.en: I stopped at the mouth of the alley and ran a quick count: three patrol arcs, two dead signal zones, one open gap near the east fence. *Overall*, the odds were not in my favor — but the gap was real, and it would close in four minutes. Ali's marker glowed faint on my scanner, just past the fence line. Four minutes was enough.
overall:1.cnHint: 我快速评估了整体____形势，发现胜算不大，但东围栏附近有一个真实的突破口，只有四分钟窗口期。
overall:1.hook: My scanner flickered once — Ali's marker had just gone dark.
overall:1.line: '*Overall* the path looks clear, but Zero controls the lights on that block.'

satisfaction:1.en: The broadcast tower loomed above the flooded street. I cracked Zero's cipher in under a minute. A quiet *satisfaction* settled in my chest — not pride, just the clean feeling of a lock giving way. Ali watched the decrypted text scroll across my screen and said nothing. That silence felt like a reward.
satisfaction:1.cnHint: 我破解了零点的密码，胸中涌起一种____。
satisfaction:1.hook: But the message inside was addressed to me.
satisfaction:1.line: 'There is a small *satisfaction* in knowing your enemy underestimated you,' Ali said.

cultivate:1.en: Grey Crow met me under the broken rail bridge, rain hammering the concrete. 'You don't find sources in Harbor City,' he said. 'You *cultivate* them — slowly, like something fragile growing in bad soil.' He pressed a data chip into my palm. Somewhere above us, Zero's drones circled the block.
cultivate:1.cnHint: 灰鸦在桥下告诉我，如何在这座城市____线人。
cultivate:1.hook: The chip was warm, as if someone had just ripped it free.
cultivate:1.line: '*Cultivate* trust before you ask for secrets,' Grey Crow warned, not looking up.

productive:1.en: Ali and I swept three blocks in forty minutes, tagging every coded sign Zero's crew had stencilled on the walls. It was the most *productive* hour I'd had since joining the unit — clean data, clear patterns, a map forming in my head. Then the lights on the whole street went out at once.
productive:1.cnHint: 阿栗和我在街上收集情报，这是最____的一个小时，直到……
productive:1.hook: In the sudden dark, someone behind us started counting down.
productive:1.line: 'Stay focused — *productive* work now saves lives later,' Ali said sharply.

vision:1.en: The fog rolled in off the harbour and swallowed the street whole. My *vision* dropped to a few metres; beyond that, only neon smears and moving shadows. I heard Zero's voice somewhere ahead, calm and close, as if the fog carried it directly to my ear. I stopped moving and listened.
vision:1.cnHint: 大雾笼罩街道，我的____只剩几米，但零点的声音清晰传来。
vision:1.hook: He was describing exactly where I was standing.
vision:1.line: 'Good *vision* is not your eyes — it is what you choose to see,' Grey Crow once told me.

distance:1.en: Zero stood at the far end of Harbour Lane. I could not read his face at that *distance*, only the still way he held his shoulders — patient, certain. Ali gripped my arm. 'He wants you to close the gap,' she whispered. 'Don't.' The lane stretched between us like a dare.
distance:1.cnHint: 零点在街道另一头，____太远，我看不清他的表情。
distance:1.hook: He raised one hand and beckoned, slowly.
distance:1.line: 'Keep your *distance* — that is how he wins,' Ali whispered into my ear.

forward:1.en: Every street in this quarter was blocked — barriers, flooded tunnels, Zero's watchers on the rooftops. There was only one way left: straight through the market crowd, lights blazing overhead, no cover. I made the decision fast. Moving *forward* was the only choice that cost me nothing I couldn't recover. I walked.
forward:1.cnHint: 四处被封锁，我决定向____走，穿过人群。
forward:1.hook: A hand caught my shoulder before I reached the first stall.
forward:1.line: 'The only safe move is *forward* — hesitation is a gift to your enemy,' Grey Crow said.

harmful:1.en: The coded graffiti looked simple — a crow, a zero, a wave. But Grey Crow pulled me back before I could photograph it. 'The ink is laced with a signal tag,' he said. 'One scan and they know your device.' Even a picture could be *harmful* here. I lowered my lens and stepped away.
harmful:1.cnHint: 格雷·克劳阻止我拍照，因为这样做可能是____的。
harmful:1.hook: My lens had already auto-scanned for half a second.
harmful:1.line: 'In this city, even looking too long can be *harmful*,' Grey Crow said quietly.

impossible:1.en: Zero had locked the bridge gate with a six-layer cipher, a crowd of rain-soaked civilians behind me, and a thirty-second window before the patrol looped back. Ali stared at the lock. 'This is *impossible*,' she breathed. I was already working, fingers moving, counting the layers down. Twenty-eight seconds. Twenty-seven.
impossible:1.cnHint: 零点设置了六层密码锁，阿栗说这____破解，但我已经开始了。
impossible:1.hook: The patrol's lights swept around the corner at twenty seconds.
impossible:1.line: '*Impossible* just means no one has been desperate enough yet,' I said, and kept working.

admit:1.en: The checkpoint gate stood between me and the lower docks. Rain hammered the iron. Grey Crow pressed a cold chip into my palm. 'Show this. They will *admit* you without question.' I walked forward, heart loud, the chip warm against my wet fingers.
admit:1.cnHint: 灰鸦给了我一枚芯片，让我能____进入下层码头的检查站。
admit:1.hook: The guard's scanner beeped once — then went silent.
admit:1.line: 'They will *admit* you, but only if you do not look back.'

association:1.en: Coded graffiti covered the bridge wall — a circle, three lines, a broken key. Ali crouched beside me, voice low. 'That mark belongs to the *Association* of Silent Channels. They run every hidden signal in this district.' I had heard the name once, in a warning.
association:1.cnHint: 阿里辨认出桥墙上的暗号，那是某个地下____留下的标记。
association:1.hook: Someone had painted it fresh — the ink was still wet.
association:1.line: 'The *Association* does not leave marks unless they want to be found.'

brand:1.en: A iron sign hung above the night market stall, its letters burned away except one. Grey Crow traced the scar on the metal. 'Every safe house in Harbor City carries this *brand* — you just have to know where the heat touched deepest.' I memorised the shape fast.
brand:1.cnHint: 灰鸦指着铁牌上的烙印告诉我，这个____是秘密据点的标志。
brand:1.hook: Behind the stall, a door opened into total darkness.
brand:1.line: 'Learn this *brand* — it is the only sign you can trust tonight.'

deep:1.en: We dropped through a service hatch into the understreet. Pipes groaned above. The passage cut *deep* beneath the market crowd, far from any camera, far from any patrol. Ali kept one hand on the wall, guiding us by touch. The air tasted of rust and old rain.
deep:1.cnHint: 我们钻入地下通道，越走越____，远离了所有摄像头。
deep:1.hook: Somewhere ahead, a single light blinked and died.
deep:1.line: 'Go *deep* enough and even Zero cannot hear your steps.'

discover:1.en: I pulled back a sheet of loose metal on the alley wall and *discovered* a row of tiny transmitters, each no bigger than a button, each still blinking. Someone had built a listening web here — patient, quiet, invisible to anyone who did not know to look.
discover:1.cnHint: 我掀开铁皮，____了一排隐藏在巷墙里的微型发射器。
discover:1.hook: One transmitter was pointed directly at our safe house.
discover:1.line: 'If Zero managed to *discover* this spot, we have very little time.'

essential:1.en: Grey Crow spread a rough map on the wet ground. Rain blurred the ink fast. 'Three exits, two power lines, one clean route out — these are the *essentials*. Forget everything else.' I pressed the details into memory before the next gust of wind erased the map entirely.
essential:1.cnHint: 灰鸦在雨中展开地图，告诉我撤退的几个____要素。
essential:1.hook: The map dissolved — but one exit was already marked with a cross.
essential:1.line: 'Speed and silence — those two are the *essentials* tonight, nothing more.'

fine:1.en: Patrol drones swept the boulevard in slow arcs. Ali touched my arm. 'Walk steady. Look *fine*.' I straightened, slowed my breath, matched the pace of every tired worker heading home under the neon. The drone passed two metres above my head and moved on without a sound.
fine:1.cnHint: 阿里提醒我保持镇定，看起来一切____，以骗过巡逻无人机。
fine:1.hook: The drone circled back — it had caught something on its scan.
fine:1.line: 'Look *fine*, keep walking, and it will pass right over you.'

largely:1.en: The street broadcast tower had gone dark. Ali checked the dead panel. 'The signal grid in this block is *largely* controlled by one relay — knock that out and Zero loses his ears across the whole east harbour.' It sounded almost too clean. In Harbor City, clean plans rarely stayed clean.
largely:1.cnHint: 阿里说，这片区域的信号网络____由一个中继站掌控，摧毁它就能让对手失明。
largely:1.hook: Then we heard Zero's voice — already on the same street.
largely:1.line: 'His network is *largely* built on one weak point — and we just found it.'

respond:1.en: Rain hammered the street. I pressed my back against the cold wall and broadcast a coded signal into the dark. Nothing. Then, forty seconds later, a light on the far roof blinked twice. Grey Crow had chosen to *respond* in the old way — no words, just light. It meant: I see you. Move now.
respond:1.cnHint: 我发出暗号信号后，灰鸦用屋顶的灯光____了，示意我立刻行动。
respond:1.hook: But the third blink never came, and the roof went dark for good.
respond:1.line: 'I will *respond* only once — so listen carefully.'

welcome:1.en: The neon arch above the east gate read HARBOR CITY in three dead languages. Nobody had repaired it in years. Ali stood beneath it, collar up, rain running off her shoulders. She gave me a short nod — the only *welcome* I was going to get in this part of town. I walked faster.
welcome:1.cnHint: 在破旧的霓虹拱门下，阿栗用一个点头给了我唯一的____，示意我快走。
welcome:1.hook: Then I noticed the shadow behind her that she clearly had not seen.
welcome:1.line: 'A nod is the only *welcome* you earn on this street.'

appeal:1.en: Zero's voice cut through the static on every public speaker along the canal road. It was a broadcast *appeal* — calm, cold, aimed at every resident who could hear: turn in the signal runner or lose power for a week. People stopped walking. They looked at each other. Then they looked at me.
appeal:1.cnHint: 零点通过广播向全体市民发出____，要求举报信号员，周围的人开始把目光投向我。
appeal:1.hook: I had about thirty seconds before someone raised a hand.
appeal:1.line: 'This *appeal* is simple: give us the runner, keep your lights.'

finally:1.en: Three nights of dead ends. Three nights of wrong tunnels and cold leads. Then, on the rain-slicked corner of Seventh and Canal, I *finally* picked up the signal I had been chasing — a short pulse buried inside the traffic noise, repeating every nine seconds. My hands stopped shaking. My mind went sharp.
finally:1.cnHint: 经过三个夜晚的徒劳追踪，我____在路口捕捉到了那个一直在寻找的隐藏信号。
finally:1.hook: The pulse shifted frequency once, then went completely silent.
finally:1.line: 'You *finally* found it — but so did someone else.'

guess:1.en: Grey Crow pulled me into a doorway and spoke low. 'The coded graffiti on the east wall — what does it mean?' I looked at the marks: a circle, three lines, an arrow. I could only *guess* from the pattern that it was a warning, not a meeting point. Grey Crow's silence told me I was right.
guess:1.cnHint: 灰鸦考我东墙上密码涂鸦的含义，我只能根据图案____它是一个警告。
guess:1.hook: Then Grey Crow said there was a second message hidden inside the first.
guess:1.line: '*Guess* wrong once out here and there is no second chance.'

protection:1.en: The signal market ran openly at night on Dry Dock Lane. Sellers offered codes, keys, hidden frequencies — and, for the right price, *protection* from Zero's broadcast sweeps. Ali had paid for that cover once. Tonight the seller's stall was empty, the awning torn, the lock cut clean. Cover was gone.
protection:1.cnHint: 阿栗曾经购买过免遭零点扫描的____，但今晚那个摊位已被洗劫一空。
protection:1.hook: Which meant Zero already knew exactly where we planned to meet.
protection:1.line: 'Without *protection*, your signal lasts maybe two minutes before they find you.'

resident:1.en: The building had been dark for a month. I climbed to the fourth floor and found one light on — a single lamp behind a fogged window. The old *resident* inside opened the door before I knocked. She already knew my face. She pressed a folded card into my hand and said nothing at all.
resident:1.cnHint: 那栋废弃楼里唯一的____在我敲门前就开了门，把一张折叠卡片塞给了我。
resident:1.hook: The card held one word, and that word was my own name.
resident:1.line: 'Every *resident* on this block has been watching you since yesterday.'

willing:1.en: I needed someone to carry the signal core across the bridge checkpoint. Ali looked at the core in my palm — small, warm, worth ten years in a labor block if caught. She was quiet for a long moment. Then she closed my fingers around it and said she was *willing*. I did not know what to say.
willing:1.cnHint: 阿栗看着那枚危险的信号核心沉默片刻后，说她____承担这次风险，我一时语塞。
willing:1.hook: Her eyes said something else entirely, and I almost asked what it was.
willing:1.line: 'I am *willing* — but you owe me the truth when this is over.'

machine:1.en: The rain hit the street like static. I crouched behind a broken vending unit on Fifth Canal. The *machine* that ran Harbor City's traffic grid sat exposed in the open — wires cut, screen dark. Someone had already been here. The silence was wrong.
machine:1.cnHint: 调查员在街头发现控制城市交通的____已被人动过手脚。
machine:1.hook: A fresh boot-print in the oil told me I was not alone.
machine:1.line: Grey Crow said, 'The *machine* does not forget who touched it last.'

observe:1.en: Ali pulled me into a doorway on Ash Street. 'We *observe* the old protocol tonight,' she said. Every agent who worked this district knew the rule: lights off, hoods up, no names spoken aloud. The neon above us buzzed and died. Then we saw the figure cross below.
observe:1.cnHint: 调查员和阿栗在街头____约定好的旧规矩，悄悄等待目标出现。
observe:1.hook: The figure stopped, turned, and looked straight up at us.
observe:1.line: Ali said, 'We *observe* the rule or we do not leave this street.'

fat:1.en: The market stalls on Copper Row were dark except for one lamp. A man with rings on every finger sat eating from a tin. Grey Crow had warned me about him — the *fat* profit he made selling signal keys meant he knew every move Zero planned. I needed him to talk.
fat:1.cnHint: 调查员在街头市场找到一个靠出卖信号密钥赚取____利润的线人。
fat:1.hook: He looked up slowly, grease on his chin, and smiled like he expected me.
fat:1.line: Grey Crow said, 'The *fat* in this city belongs to those who hold the keys.'

helpful:1.en: Zero's courier dropped a folded card on the wet pavement of Bridge Lane and walked on without slowing. I picked it up. The card was blank except for a single coordinate. It was almost *helpful* — almost. Any lead Zero left in the open was also a trap. I stood still and thought.
helpful:1.cnHint: 调查员捡到零点留下的线索卡片，这个____的提示很可能是个圈套。
helpful:1.hook: Across the lane, a shadow peeled itself off the wall and moved toward me.
helpful:1.line: Ali said, 'That card is only *helpful* if you already know what it costs.'

position:1.en: Grey Crow met me under the broken clock at North Wharf. He pointed up at the roof line. 'Zero has taken a *position* on the high platform — clear view of the whole square.' My throat tightened. From that height Zero could track anyone. There was no cover worth trusting below.
position:1.cnHint: 灰鸦告诉调查员，零点已经占据了广场上方的有利____，可以监视一切。
position:1.hook: The clock above us gave one dead tick, then stopped forever.
position:1.line: Grey Crow said, 'That *position* gives Zero every exit in a single glance.'

threat:1.en: A line of coded graffiti ran down the wall of Transit Alley — fresh paint, still wet. Ali read it faster than I could. 'It is a *threat*,' she said quietly. 'Signed by Zero. Directed at anyone who reports to the bureau tonight.' My hand went to my collar comm and stayed there.
threat:1.cnHint: 涂鸦巷里出现了零点留下的____，警告所有向当局报告的人。
threat:1.hook: Somewhere behind the wall, a door opened with a sound like a held breath.
threat:1.line: Ali said, 'A *threat* written in public means Zero wants us frightened before we act.'

trend:1.en: I had tracked every move Zero made over the past six weeks. The pattern was clear once you mapped it: each strike was closer to the Central Relay. Grey Crow called it a *trend* toward control — whoever held the Relay held the city's voice. Tonight the line finally reached its end point.
trend:1.cnHint: 调查员发现零点的行动有一个明显的____，每次都更靠近城市的核心中继站。
trend:1.hook: The Central Relay tower blinked once on the skyline, then went completely dark.
trend:1.line: Grey Crow said, 'This *trend* ends at the Relay — or it ends us.'

ultimately:1.en: Ali and I split at the East Gate. Every route we had traced, every coded signal we had cracked, every risk we had taken in the wet streets of Harbor City — it all led here. *Ultimately*, the city would survive or fall on what happened in the next ten minutes. I stepped forward.
ultimately:1.cnHint: 调查员意识到一切调查和冒险____都指向此刻的决定性行动。
ultimately:1.hook: The gate swung open before I touched it — someone knew I was coming.
ultimately:1.line: Ali said, 'We *ultimately* answer for this city, you and I, right now.'

slightly:1.en: The rain had stopped. I moved through the market alley, my coat *slightly* damp from the last shower. Grey Crow waited near a broken lamp post, eyes scanning the crowd. Something was off. The stalls were too quiet, the vendors too still. Someone had cleared this street before we arrived.
slightly:1.cnHint: 我穿过市场小巷，感觉气氛不对，灰鸦已在等我，街道____ 有些异样。
slightly:1.hook: Grey Crow whispered one word, then vanished into the dark.
slightly:1.line: 'The air feels *slightly* wrong — someone swept this street clean.'

vital:1.en: Grey Crow pressed a folded note into my hand between two market stalls. 'This address,' he said. Outside, coded graffiti covered every wall. One symbol matched the note exactly. That symbol was *vital* — without it, the whole network of hidden drops stayed invisible to any outsider trying to map them.
vital:1.cnHint: 灰鸦给了我一张纸条，上面的地址对整个行动____。
vital:1.hook: The symbol began to fade, as if the wall itself was erasing it.
vital:1.line: 'That mark is *vital* — lose it and we lose everything.'

mention:1.en: Ali caught up with me at the edge of the night market, out of breath. She had heard a broadcast — scrambled, but clear enough. There was one *mention* of my name inside it, buried between static and noise. One mention was enough. Zero knew I was here, and Zero never warned without reason.
mention:1.cnHint: 阿栗听到一段广播，里面有一次对我名字的____，这让我们都紧张起来。
mention:1.hook: Ali grabbed my arm: 'That broadcast is still looping.'
mention:1.line: 'One *mention* of your name — Zero put it there on purpose.'

rare:1.en: The upper streets of Harbor City were almost empty at this hour. Clean air up here was *rare*; most nights the smog sat heavy over the lower markets. I spotted Zero standing on a bridge above the transit lines, coat still, watching me. He had chosen this spot carefully. High ground. Clear sight.
rare:1.cnHint: 高处街道的清洁空气____，零点就站在那里的桥上，居高临下地注视着我。
rare:1.hook: Zero raised one hand — not a wave, a signal to someone behind me.
rare:1.line: 'Clear air is *rare* up here — enjoy it while you can.'

useful:1.en: Ali handed me a small drive she had pulled from a crack in the market wall. 'Could be nothing,' she said. I turned it over. It was warm, recently placed. Grey Crow had told me that old drops like this were still *useful* — the network hid its most sensitive data in the lowest-tech spots.
useful:1.cnHint: 阿栗找到一个藏在墙缝里的小设备，灰鸦说这类旧藏点依然____。
useful:1.hook: The drive's single light blinked once, then held steady.
useful:1.line: 'Old drops are still *useful* — Zero's crew forgot about them.'

blood:1.en: I crouched by the base of a lamp post at the transit plaza. There was a thin line of red on the ground, still wet. Not much, but enough. Grey Crow appeared beside me without a sound. 'Fresh,' he said. Someone had been here seconds ago. *Blood* on a clean street meant the operation had already started.
blood:1.cnHint: 我在广场灯柱旁发现了地上新鲜的____，灰鸦说行动已经开始了。
blood:1.hook: Somewhere above us, a door slammed shut with a heavy echo.
blood:1.line: '*Blood* on a clean street — we are already too late to stop this.'

fund:1.en: The hacked billboard above the market was cycling through numbers. Ali read them fast. 'That is a transfer sequence,' she said. Someone was moving a hidden *fund* through the public display network in plain sight, encoded as an advertisement. Grey Crow had warned me about this trick. Tonight it was running live.
fund:1.cnHint: 市场上方的广告牌正在转移一笔隐藏的____，就藏在所有人看得见的数字里。
fund:1.hook: The sequence ended, and every light on the street cut out at once.
fund:1.line: 'They are moving the *fund* right now — through the billboard above you.'

anxiety:1.en: I stood at the far end of the harbor road, waiting for Grey Crow's signal. Minutes passed. The silence fed my *anxiety* — each second without contact meant another second Zero had to move. Ali said nothing beside me, but I could hear her breathing, quick and shallow. We were both counting the same clock.
anxiety:1.cnHint: 我们在海港路等待信号，漫长的沉默加深了我的____，零点也许正在利用这段时间行动。
anxiety:1.hook: Then my receiver crackled, and Grey Crow's voice came through, broken and strange.
anxiety:1.line: 'Your *anxiety* is loud — Zero can read it from across the street.'

meaning:1.en: The coded graffiti covered the bridge wall for three blocks. Most people walked past without a second look. But I could hear a low signal beneath the paint, and the *meaning* of the symbols hit me all at once: a map. A map to Zero's next drop point.
meaning:1.cnHint: 调查员发现桥墙上涂鸦的____，那是一张指向零点下一个据点的地图。
meaning:1.hook: The drop point was only two streets away, and someone was already moving toward it.
meaning:1.line: 'The *meaning* of those symbols is a map — and Zero drew it.'

strengthen:1.en: Rain had washed half the signal away. Ali crouched beside me under the overpass, pressing a small relay device against the wet concrete. 'This will *strengthen* the broadcast enough to trace,' she said. The device hummed. Then the hum stopped, and we heard footsteps above us.
strengthen:1.cnHint: 阿栗用设备____了信号，但头顶突然传来了脚步声。
strengthen:1.hook: Whoever was up there had stopped walking directly over our heads.
strengthen:1.line: 'I need sixty seconds to *strengthen* the signal — hold them off.'

competitive:1.en: Zero never acted alone. I had learned that the hard way. In Harbor City, information was the most *competitive* market of all — every crew, every fixer, every shadow broker fighting for the same encrypted data streams. Tonight, two other groups had shown up at the canal. Zero had sold the same tip twice.
competitive:1.cnHint: 调查员意识到零点把情报卖给了两个不同的团伙，因为信息是这座城市里____性最强的商品。
competitive:1.hook: Both rival groups had just noticed each other across the dark water.
competitive:1.line: 'This city runs on the most *competitive* trade there is — secrets.'

recently:1.en: The neon signs along Dock Row flickered in a pattern I had not seen before. Grey Crow had warned me about this. '*Recently*,' they had said, 'Zero has been embedding new codes in the light cycles — watch the red signs, not the blue.' I watched. The red signs spelled out three letters: R-U-N.
recently:1.cnHint: 灰鸦告诉调查员，零点____开始把密码藏进霓虹灯的闪烁节奏里，红色灯牌拼出了三个字母。
recently:1.hook: I ran, and the explosion came four seconds later.
recently:1.line: '*Recently* Zero changed the code — the red signs are the ones that matter.'

nation:1.en: The broadcast was not meant for one crew or one city. I filtered the signal through my receiver and felt it spread — wide, structured, layered. This was a message aimed at every dark network in the *nation*, a call to move against the Signal Authority at once. Grey Crow had said it would come. I had not believed them until now.
nation:1.cnHint: 调查员破译了一段广播，发现这是发给全____地下网络的集结信号。
nation:1.hook: Someone had already sent the reply, and it was not me.
nation:1.line: 'This signal reaches every corner of the *nation* — Zero is done hiding.'

perceive:1.en: Ordinary people could not *perceive* the sub-layer frequencies buried in the city's public address system. I could. Standing at the corner of Grid Nine and Canal South, I heard Zero's voice beneath the weather report, calm and close, as if they were standing right beside me. 'You are late,' the voice said.
perceive:1.cnHint: 调查员能____到公共广播系统下层隐藏的频率，听见了零点的声音。
perceive:1.hook: I turned around, and the corner behind me was empty — but still warm.
perceive:1.line: 'Most people cannot *perceive* what is hidden in plain sound — you can.'

pound:1.en: The signal repeater was sealed inside a metal box bolted to the base of the harbor wall. Ali handed me a short steel bar without a word. I had to *pound* the lock three times before it cracked open. Inside, still blinking, was a drive tagged with Zero's mark — and a countdown timer showing nine minutes.
pound:1.cnHint: 调查员用力____开锁，在金属箱里发现了零点留下的驱动器和一个倒计时装置。
pound:1.hook: Nine minutes was not enough time to reach the safe house on foot.
pound:1.line: '*Pound* it harder — we have eight minutes left and I am not leaving empty-handed.'

purpose:1.en: Grey Crow met me at the far end of the night market, between a dim noodle stand and a wall of dead screens. They pressed a folded card into my hand. On it was a single sentence in plain text — no code, no cipher. 'Every signal has a *purpose*,' it read, 'and this one was meant to find you.' I looked up. Grey Crow was already gone.
purpose:1.cnHint: 灰鸦给了调查员一张卡片，上面写着每个信号都有其____，而这个信号是专门为找到调查员而设计的。
purpose:1.hook: On the back of the card, in tiny print, was my own home address.
purpose:1.line: 'Every signal has a *purpose*, and yours just revealed exactly who you are.'

digital:1.en: Rain hammered the street. A wall of cracked screens lined the alley, each one running stolen feeds. I pressed close and watched the *digital* noise shift — hidden inside the static, a map of Zero's next move. Grey Crow had said the signal would be there. She was right.
digital:1.cnHint: 我在充满破旧屏幕的小巷里，从____噪音中发现了零点的行动地图。
digital:1.hook: The map blinked once, then vanished.
digital:1.line: 'That *digital* noise is not random — read it again.'

sale:1.en: A street vendor had set up under a flickering lamp, crates stacked high. The sign read: FINAL *SALE*. Ali elbowed me. Every item on that table was marked with a small red crow — Grey Crow's signal. Someone was moving stolen data right here in the open.
sale:1.cnHint: 街边摊位打着____的招牌，阿栗发现每件货物上都有灰鸦的暗号。
sale:1.hook: The vendor's eyes locked on mine and did not blink.
sale:1.line: 'It is not a real *sale* — those crates hold something worse than goods.'

contact:1.en: I crossed the wet square alone, hood low. Grey Crow had told me to *contact* no one until I reached the old clock tower. But halfway across, my receiver buzzed — one short pulse. Ali. She had found something. The rule was already broken.
contact:1.cnHint: 我独自穿过广场，但阿栗在我____她之前就先发来了信号。
contact:1.hook: A second pulse came — and then silence.
contact:1.line: 'Do not *contact* me on this channel — Zero is listening.'

failure:1.en: The gate was supposed to be open. It was not. I rattled the lock, then stepped back, reading the rust on the hinges. This was not my *failure* — the gate had been sealed from the inside, recently. Someone had got here first and locked the way out.
failure:1.cnHint: 约定的大门紧闭，这不是我的____，有人抢先一步封住了出口。
failure:1.hook: A shadow moved behind the frosted glass above me.
failure:1.line: '*Failure* to reach that roof means we lose everything tonight.'

bird:1.en: A lone crow landed on the wire above the crossroads, black against the yellow haze. Ali grabbed my sleeve. 'Grey Crow uses a real *bird* as a signal,' she whispered. I looked up. The crow tilted its head once to the left. North. We changed direction without a word.
bird:1.cnHint: 一只真正的____落在路口电线上，成为灰鸦给我们的方向暗号。
bird:1.hook: The crow lifted off — heading straight toward Zero's block.
bird:1.line: 'When you see that *bird*, you move — no questions, no delay.'

official:1.en: A black car sat parked at the corner, engine off, no plates. Standing beside it was a man in a grey coat — the kind that said *official* without a single word on it. I kept walking, eyes ahead. Grey Crow had warned me: some enemies wear the city itself as a badge.
official:1.cnHint: 路口停着一辆黑色无牌车，旁边站着一个散发____气息的灰衣男人。
official:1.hook: He turned his head exactly as I passed.
official:1.line: 'That man is no low *official* — he answers to the top floor.'

confidence:1.en: Zero stepped out of the doorway into the rain like he owned the street, shoulders loose, pace slow. That kind of *confidence* was a weapon — it made bystanders look away and kept hands off triggers. I steadied my breath. He had not seen me yet. One moment was all I needed.
confidence:1.cnHint: 零点带着令人不安的____走入雨中，我屏住呼吸，等待那一个瞬间。
confidence:1.hook: He stopped — and smiled at the exact wall I hid behind.
confidence:1.line: 'His *confidence* means he already knows where you are standing.'

display:1.en: The large screen above the market entrance flickered and changed. Instead of the usual city news, it began to *display* a single line of white text on black — coordinates, repeating on a loop. People below barely looked up. But I knew the font. It was Grey Crow's hand.
display:1.cnHint: 市场入口的大屏幕开始____一行坐标，那是灰鸦留给我的信息。
display:1.hook: The text looped three times — then the screen cracked dark.
display:1.line: 'She chose to *display* it in public — she had no safer way left.'

awareness:1.en: The rain hit the street in sheets. I moved through the crowd, every nerve alive. My *awareness* of the signal grew sharper with each step — a low hum hidden inside the neon signs above me. Grey Crow had warned me: in Harbor City, the ones who stop noticing are the ones who disappear.
awareness:1.cnHint: 调查员在街头人群中行走，对隐藏信号的____越来越强烈。
awareness:1.hook: The hum shifted — and now it had my name.
awareness:1.line: 'Your *awareness* is your only shield out here,' Grey Crow said.

introduce:1.en: Ali pulled me into a side alley off the main boulevard. 'They don't know you yet,' she whispered. 'Let me *introduce* you as a signal trader — nothing more.' Rain pooled at our feet. Across the street, Zero's scouts were already watching every face that passed under the broken lamps.
introduce:1.cnHint: 阿栗计划在街头把调查员____给危险人物，掩护身份。
introduce:1.hook: Zero's scout turned — and looked straight at us.
introduce:1.line: 'I'll *introduce* you, but say nothing after that,' Ali warned.

expense:1.en: The market stalls along Wharf Row burned with cheap neon. Grey Crow spread a stolen map across a wet crate. 'Zero rebuilt his whole network at great *expense*,' he said, tracing a red line with one finger. 'That means he can't afford to let us reach the eastern relay tower.'
expense:1.cnHint: 灰鸦在码头街边解释，零点为重建网络付出了巨大的____。
expense:1.hook: A shadow fell across the map — from behind us.
expense:1.line: 'At this *expense*, Zero will protect that tower with everything,' Grey Crow said.

toward:1.en: The street split at the iron bridge. I watched Zero's courier break from the crowd and move *toward* the old transit hall, a sealed data chip pressed inside one closed fist. Ali touched my arm once — the signal to follow. The rain fell harder. Every step I took felt like a point of no return.
toward:1.cnHint: 调查员看见零点的信使朝某个方向走去，决定跟踪。
toward:1.hook: The courier stopped, turned, and stared back at me.
toward:1.line: 'Move *toward* the hall — slow and natural,' Ali said quietly.

track:1.en: Broken rail lines ran along the edge of Sector Nine. Grey Crow crouched low and pressed two fingers to the old *track*, reading vibrations the way others read words. 'Someone heavy passed here twelve minutes ago,' he said without looking up. Above us, a surveillance drone circled once, then went dark.
track:1.cnHint: 灰鸦在废弃轨道旁，通过____上的震动追踪可疑人物。
track:1.hook: The drone going dark was not a glitch — it was a signal.
track:1.line: 'This *track* tells me Zero was here first,' Grey Crow said.

afford:1.en: Street vendors were packing up fast, reading the night the way animals read weather. 'We can't *afford* to wait for backup,' Ali said, her eyes fixed on the far end of Canal Street. The relay device in my coat pocket was already warm — it had been active for too long. Time was the one thing Zero was stealing from us.
afford:1.cnHint: 阿栗警告调查员，他们已经____不起继续等待了。
afford:1.hook: Then every light on Canal Street cut out at once.
afford:1.line: 'We can't *afford* another wrong move tonight,' Ali said.

feature:1.en: Rain blurred every face on the bridge. But one detail held my eye: a small scar — the key *feature* that Grey Crow had described — just below the left ear of a figure leaning against the railing. Zero's handler. Real, breathing, three meters away. I steadied my breath and kept walking as if I had seen nothing.
feature:1.cnHint: 调查员在桥上通过一个关键____，认出了零点的联络人。
feature:1.hook: The figure pushed off the railing and fell into step behind me.
feature:1.line: 'That scar is the one *feature* you cannot miss,' Grey Crow had said.

innovative:1.en: The device Zero had planted under the market bridge was small and almost invisible — more *innovative* than anything our department had seen. Ali photographed it from three angles without touching it. 'Whoever built this is not working alone,' she said. Below us the canal ran black, carrying neon reflections toward the open sea.
innovative:1.cnHint: 阿栗发现了零点安置的极具____性的装置，断定背后另有高人。
innovative:1.hook: Ali's camera blinked red — the device had just activated.
innovative:1.line: 'This is too *innovative* for Zero to have made alone,' Ali said.

institution:1.en: The rain-slicked street outside the old data vault smelled of rust and burnt wire. Grey Crow pointed at the cracked seal above the gate. 'This *institution* once set the rules for every broadcast in Harbor City,' he said. Now it was dark. Someone had erased it from every public record.
institution:1.cnHint: 灰鸦指着一栋废弃建筑的封印，告诉我这个____曾掌控全城广播。
institution:1.hook: Its last signal was still looping, somewhere underground.
institution:1.line: 'This *institution* wrote the laws that kept us all silent.'

outcome:1.en: Ali crouched beside the storm drain, fingers tracing the coded marks left in chalk on the curb. Three symbols, one warning. She had seen this pattern before and knew what it meant for us. The *outcome* of ignoring it was printed on a torn poster ten steps away: a list of names, all crossed out.
outcome:1.cnHint: 阿里在路边发现暗号，上面的____让我们不寒而栗。
outcome:1.hook: My name was not on the list — not yet.
outcome:1.line: 'The *outcome* of this mission is already written on that wall.'

recognize:1.en: Zero stood under a buzzing neon sign, hood up, face turned away. I had been tracking this person for six days. Then the figure shifted and the light hit their jaw. I could *recognize* that scar anywhere — I had seen it in a file marked classified, on a face declared dead two years ago.
recognize:1.cnHint: 我在霓虹灯下终于____出了那个据说已死之人的面孔。
recognize:1.hook: The dead do not usually check their watch and walk away.
recognize:1.line: 'You *recognize* me — which means you have read things you should not have.'

safety:1.en: The bridge was the only way out of the lower district. Ali grabbed my sleeve as we stepped onto the wet steel. 'Move fast and stay low,' she said. Halfway across, the lamp posts went dark one by one. *Safety* on this bridge was a rumor; the far end was swallowed by fog and silence.
safety:1.cnHint: 我们穿越大桥时，____变成了一种奢望，黑暗从四面逼近。
safety:1.hook: Something heavy landed on the bridge behind us.
safety:1.line: '*Safety* ends where the lights do — keep running.'

collect:1.en: Grey Crow moved along the alley wall, pulling small metal chips from cracks in the brick. Each chip held a fragment of a banned broadcast, hidden here over months. He had taught me to *collect* these pieces without touching them bare-handed — the signal could burn a reader who was not prepared.
collect:1.cnHint: 灰鸦沿着小巷墙壁____那些藏有禁播信号碎片的芯片。
collect:1.hook: The last chip was warm — someone had placed it there minutes ago.
collect:1.line: 'We *collect* what the city tries to bury, one chip at a time.'

door:1.en: Every building on Canal Row looked the same at midnight: sealed, dark, forgotten. Then I saw it — one *door* standing open two centimeters, a thin line of red light cutting the wet pavement. Grey Crow had marked it with a chalk triangle. This was the place. This was where Zero kept the archive.
door:1.cnHint: 运河街上一扇微开的____透出红光，那里藏着零的秘密档案。
door:1.hook: From inside came the sound of a file being deleted.
door:1.line: 'That *door* has been open for exactly three minutes — move now.'

eventually:1.en: Zero's jamming signal had been blocking us for two days. Ali rerouted our decoder through four dead relay towers, then a fifth. I watched the screen flicker, fail, flicker again. *Eventually* the static broke and a single clean voice came through the noise — calm, recorded, and addressed to me by name.
eventually:1.cnHint: 阿里一次次尝试绕过干扰，____成功截获了一段针对我的秘密录音。
eventually:1.hook: The voice said: 'You were never meant to find this.'
eventually:1.line: '*Eventually* every locked signal finds someone willing to listen.'

match:1.en: Zero stepped out of the shadow at the end of the market lane, arms loose, eyes steady. Grey Crow had warned me: in a battle of coded language and quick thinking, very few people could *match* this opponent. I had one advantage — Zero did not yet know what I had collected from the bridge.
match:1.cnHint: 零出现在街道尽头，几乎没人能在智谋上与之____，但我握有底牌。
match:1.hook: Zero smiled first, and that was never a good sign.
match:1.line: 'Find someone who can *match* Zero and you will find someone worth fearing.'

operation:1.en: Rain hammered the street outside the code market. Grey Crow handed me a folded card. 'This *operation* runs on three signals,' he said. 'Miss one, and the whole chain breaks.' I scanned the card. Each signal was a single forbidden word, written in ink that faded as I read. The third word vanished before I could memorise it.
operation:1.cnHint: 灰鸦向我说明这次____的三个关键信号，但第三个信号在我读完之前就消失了。
operation:1.hook: Somewhere in the crowd, a receiver was already listening.
operation:1.line: 'This *operation* runs on three signals — miss one, and everything breaks.'

population:1.en: The neon census board flickered above the canal. It listed Harbor City's *population* at nine million, but Ali shook her head. 'Six million of those names are ghost accounts,' she said quietly. 'Fake identities the signal network uses to hide real messages.' I looked at the number again. The city was half empty, and I had never noticed.
population:1.cnHint: 阿栗告诉我，城市____中有数百万个虚假身份被用来掩盖真实信号。
population:1.hook: One of those ghost names was mine.
population:1.line: 'The *population* count is a lie — half those names are just signal covers.'

quick:1.en: Zero's broadcast lasted four seconds. I caught it on the corner of Fifth and Rain, a *quick* pulse buried inside the traffic noise. Ali had told me Zero never repeated a signal. I replayed it in my head twice, pulling out the hidden word. It pointed to the old port. I was already moving before the echo faded.
quick:1.cnHint: 我在街角捕捉到零点发出的一个____信号，它指向旧港口。
quick:1.hook: At the old port, a light blinked once and went dark.
quick:1.line: 'A *quick* pulse like that means Zero is already at the target.'

scale:1.en: The graffiti covered the entire east wall of the underpass, but its meaning only appeared at the right *scale*. Step too close and it looked like noise. Step back ten metres and the letters locked together: a date, a district, a single name. Ali stood beside me, silent. The name on the wall was Grey Crow's.
scale:1.cnHint: 涂鸦的含义只有在正确的____下才能看清，而那个名字让我们沉默了。
scale:1.hook: Grey Crow was supposed to be on our side.
scale:1.line: 'At this *scale* the pattern becomes a message — and that message is a warning.'

basic:1.en: 'You are missing the *basic* rule of this city,' Grey Crow said, not looking at me. We stood in the open market where signal traders sold coded words for food tokens. 'Every message has a price. Every word costs something. The ones that cost nothing are the ones that will trap you.' A vendor nearby switched off his board and walked away fast.
basic:1.cnHint: 灰鸦提醒我忽视了这座城市信号交易的____规则，那些免费的词语最危险。
basic:1.hook: The vendor who left had been selling my name all morning.
basic:1.line: 'The *basic* rule here is simple: free words are always the most dangerous.'

constantly:1.en: The signal towers above the harbour *constantly* shifted frequency, never resting on one channel long enough to be locked. I had been tracking Zero's pattern for six hours. Ali sent me a short burst: 'Pattern found.' Three towers always shifted in the same order. That order was a word. The word was an address. I wrote it on my hand in the rain.
constantly:1.cnHint: 信号塔____在变换频率，但阿栗发现了零点留在其中的规律。
constantly:1.hook: The address on my hand was the building I was already standing in front of.
constantly:1.line: 'The towers *constantly* shift, but the order underneath never changes.'

favor:1.en: Zero left a message in the storm drain glyph outside the transit hall. Most investigators would *favor* the direct route — read the top layer, follow the arrow. I read the shadow layer instead, the one printed in heat ink, only visible in cold rain. It pointed the opposite direction. Zero was testing whether I was like the others.
favor:1.cnHint: 零点留下的信息有两层，我选择了大多数调查员不会____的那条隐藏路线。
favor:1.hook: The opposite direction led straight to a locked room with my name on the door.
favor:1.line: 'Smart investigators *favor* the shadow layer — Zero counts on the others missing it.'

absence:1.en: The broadcast should have carried twelve tones. I counted eleven. The *absence* of the last tone was the message itself. Ali had taught me that trick in the first week: silence can carry more data than sound. I noted the missing tone's position — seventh from the end — and cross-checked the cipher table on my sleeve. It decoded to one word: run.
absence:1.cnHint: 广播中一个音调的____才是真正的信息，解码后只有一个词：逃跑。
absence:1.hook: I ran, and behind me the street dissolved into static.
absence:1.line: 'The *absence* of that final tone is not an error — it is the whole message.'

advice:1.en: Rain hammered the street outside Zero's last known drop point. Grey Crow pulled me into a doorway and spoke low. 'My *advice*: walk away now. This signal is bait.' I checked my scanner. Three hidden nodes blinked back. He was right — and wrong. Walking away was exactly what Zero wanted.
advice:1.cnHint: 灰鸦在街头给我一个____，但我发现情况远比他说的复杂。
advice:1.hook: The scanner showed a fourth node — one Grey Crow never mentioned.
advice:1.line: 'My *advice*: walk away now, before the signal locks onto you.'

attempt:1.en: Zero's crew had tagged every wall on Ninth Street with coded graffiti. I watched Ali *attempt* to decode the third symbol, her fingers tracing neon lines in the wet air. She tried four times. Each failure triggered a soft alarm click from the wall itself. The street was listening.
attempt:1.cnHint: 阿栗在霓虹街头____破译涂鸦密码，却每次都触发警报。
attempt:1.hook: On the fifth try, the wall cracked open instead of clicking.
attempt:1.line: 'I'll *attempt* the third symbol — just keep watch and stay quiet.'

draw:1.en: Ali and I reached the crossroads at the same moment Zero's signal did. Every scanner in range locked to the same frequency. Pure *draw* — neither side could move first. Neon signs buzzed overhead. Rain filled the silence. Then Grey Crow's voice cut through the static from somewhere above us.
draw:1.cnHint: 我和零点的信号在十字路口形成____，双方都无法率先行动。
draw:1.hook: Grey Crow's voice said one word, then the frequency went dead.
draw:1.line: 'It's a *draw* — nobody moves until I say the word.'

facility:1.en: The old harbor *facility* had been shut for thirty years, but its lights were on tonight. Ali pointed at the loading dock where shadows moved between rusted containers. 'Zero is using it as a relay,' she whispered. Outside, coded broadcasts pulsed from every broken window like a heartbeat that refused to stop.
facility:1.cnHint: 废弃的港口____今夜灯火通明，成为零点中转信号的据点。
facility:1.hook: One shadow stopped moving and turned to face us directly.
facility:1.line: 'This *facility* has been dead for years — so why is it broadcasting?'

firm:1.en: Zero's message came through the street speaker in plain English, which was rare and wrong. Grey Crow's jaw was *firm*, his eyes cold as he listened. 'Don't trust a word,' he said. I recorded every syllable anyway. In Harbor City, even a trap carries truth if you know how to cut it open.
firm:1.cnHint: 灰鸦态度____，警告我不要相信零点通过街头广播传来的明文消息。
firm:1.hook: The recording contained six seconds that Grey Crow had not heard.
firm:1.line: 'Stay *firm* — do not react, no matter what that voice says.'

innovation:1.en: The coded graffiti on Canal Street was new. Ali called it Zero's latest *innovation*: symbols that shifted meaning depending on which light hit them. Red neon read one command; blue neon read the opposite. I photographed both. Somewhere in that contradiction was the real message, and I had maybe ten minutes to find it.
innovation:1.cnHint: 零点在运河街留下的涂鸦是一种新____，符号在不同灯光下含义截然相反。
innovation:1.hook: My camera found a third reading no light was supposed to create.
innovation:1.line: 'This *innovation* is clever — the message changes with every color of light.'

multiple:1.en: Grey Crow spread a worn map across the hood of a parked vehicle. *Multiple* paths led from the harbor to Zero's last broadcast point, and each one was marked with a small red cross. 'Every route is watched,' he said quietly. Ali traced one unmarked line with her finger. It led straight into the water.
multiple:1.cnHint: 地图上有____条通往零点据点的路线，但每条都被监视，只有一条没有标记。
multiple:1.hook: The unmarked line ended at a door drawn beneath the waterline.
multiple:1.line: '*Multiple* paths, all watched — except the one that should not exist.'

path:1.en: The *path* between the market stalls on Wire Row was barely wide enough for one person. Grey Crow had told me to take it only in an emergency. Tonight qualified. I moved fast, head low, scanner off to avoid pings. Halfway through, a figure stepped out of the steam ahead and stopped. Waiting.
path:1.cnHint: 我紧急走上Wire Row市场中一条狭窄的____，却在中途遭遇了拦路之人。
path:1.hook: The figure raised one hand and held up Grey Crow's badge.
path:1.line: 'This *path* is only for emergencies — so tell me what went wrong.'

safe:1.en: The alley smelled of rust and old rain. Grey Crow pointed at the wall behind a broken vent. 'There,' he said. A *safe* was welded into the concrete, its dial scratched by years of desperate hands. Whatever Zero was protecting lived inside that locked steel box.
safe:1.cnHint: 灰鸦在巷子里指出墙中藏有一个____，里面锁着零点的秘密。
safe:1.hook: The dial moved one click — from the inside.
safe:1.line: 'That *safe* holds the only copy of the signal key.'

speed:1.en: Ali pulled me onto the back of her electric runner. The city blurred into streaks of neon and wet asphalt. I checked the dash — the *speed* hit one-eighty and kept climbing. Behind us, Zero's patrol drones closed the gap with cold, mechanical patience. Outrunning them was already a fading hope.
speed:1.cnHint: 阿栗驾车以极快的____逃离，但无人机仍在追近。
speed:1.hook: One drone locked on — and fired a net.
speed:1.line: 'At this *speed* we have maybe forty seconds before they catch us.'

burden:1.en: Grey Crow stopped at the checkpoint bridge and handed me a steel case. His shoulders dropped the moment it left his hands. 'Carry it across,' he said quietly. I felt the weight shift to me — not just the case, but the *burden* of everything he had carried alone for three years.
burden:1.cnHint: 灰鸦将沉重的____转交给我，我感受到了他三年来独自承担的压力。
burden:1.hook: The checkpoint light turned red the instant I stepped forward.
burden:1.line: 'This *burden* was never meant for one person alone.'

former:1.en: Two routes lay on the map: the harbour tunnel or the elevated rail. Grey Crow tapped the *former* without hesitation. 'The tunnel is older. Fewer sensors.' I studied the route lines. He was right — the first choice was darker and narrower, but it offered one thing the second could not: silence.
former:1.cnHint: 面对两条路线，灰鸦选择了____，因为那里传感器更少。
former:1.hook: The tunnel entrance, however, was already sealed shut.
former:1.line: 'Take the *former* route — the rail is already watched.'

oppose:1.en: A crowd had blocked the junction outside the data tower. They held signs with scrambled letters — coded protest. I tried to move through. A tall figure in grey stepped forward to *oppose* my path, arms wide, eyes steady. It was not aggression. It was a warning dressed as a wall.
oppose:1.cnHint: 在数据塔外，一个神秘人物出面____我前进，像是一道无声的警告。
oppose:1.hook: Behind the wall of people, Zero was already watching me.
oppose:1.line: 'I don't *oppose* you — I'm trying to keep you alive.'

unable:1.en: The signal jammer hit without sound. My comm went dark, my map froze, and I stood in the middle of the market street completely *unable* to call for help or find my bearing. Stalls buzzed around me. Strangers moved like shadows. I was alone in a city that had just gone silent.
unable:1.cnHint: 信号干扰器让我____呼救或确认方向，只能孤立无援地站在街头。
unable:1.hook: Then someone slipped a folded note into my coat pocket.
unable:1.line: 'If you're *unable* to reach Ali, follow the green lamp posts.'

unusual:1.en: Nothing about the street looked wrong at first. Then I noticed: every shop sign faced the same direction. Every parked vehicle had its window cracked exactly one inch. Grey Crow touched my arm. 'See it?' he murmured. The pattern was *unusual* enough to mean one thing — someone had arranged this scene on purpose.
unusual:1.cnHint: 街道上一切看似正常，却有一种____的规律暗示着人为布置。
unusual:1.hook: At the far end of the street, a figure vanished into a door.
unusual:1.line: '*Unusual* arrangements like this are Zero's signature — run.'

apart:1.en: Ali and I had entered the district together, but the crowd separated us near the overpass. I turned and she was gone — just bodies and noise where she had been. We were *apart* now by at least three city blocks, and my comm was showing her signal drifting further with every second.
apart:1.cnHint: 我和阿栗在天桥附近失散，彼此____，她的信号正在不断飘远。
apart:1.hook: Her signal stopped moving — suddenly and completely.
apart:1.line: 'Stay *apart* from me — they're tracking anyone I stand near.'

character:1.en: The rain-soaked wall held a single burned mark — a *character* that Grey Crow said the city's old code-writers used as a warning sign. I traced it with one finger. The ink felt warm, almost alive. Ali pulled my hand back fast.
character:1.cnHint: 灰鸦说墙上那个____是古老的警告符号，我伸手触碰，阿里猛地拉开我。
character:1.hook: Warm ink on a cold wall meant someone had been here seconds ago.
character:1.line: 'That *character* is a trap trigger,' Grey Crow said, voice flat.

clean:1.en: Zero's crew had swept the alley bare — no wrappers, no boot marks, nothing. The pavement was *clean* in a way that Harbor City streets never are. Ali crouched low and whispered that only one kind of person scrubs a crime scene this well.
clean:1.cnHint: 阿里蹲下来说，这条小巷被清理得____，这在海港城从来不正常。
clean:1.hook: A city this dirty is never spotless without a reason.
clean:1.line: 'Too *clean*,' Ali said. 'They knew we were coming.'

convey:1.en: Grey Crow did not speak. Instead he held up three fingers, then tapped the street lamp twice. Every rookie learns that silent signals *convey* more than words when Zero's listeners are near. I nodded. We moved before the light changed.
convey:1.cnHint: 灰鸦用手势____信息，因为附近可能有零的监听器。
convey:1.hook: The lamp flickered once — a reply from someone we could not see.
convey:1.line: 'A good signal can *convey* more than a shout,' Grey Crow said.

distraction:1.en: A food cart burst into sparks at the far end of the block. Ali grabbed my collar. 'That fire is a *distraction*,' he said. While every eye turned toward the smoke, Zero's courier slipped through the crowd behind us, close enough to brush my shoulder.
distraction:1.cnHint: 街尾突然起火，阿里警告我那只是____，真正的危险在我们身后。
distraction:1.hook: The courier was already gone before the smoke cleared.
distraction:1.line: 'Don't move — the fire is just a *distraction*,' Ali said.

fight:1.en: Grey Crow walked toward Zero's two guards without slowing down. He had no weapon I could see, only the quiet *fight* in his eyes that made hard men step aside. They stepped aside. Ali and I followed before either of us thought to breathe.
fight:1.cnHint: 灰鸦眼神中的____让两个守卫默默让路，我和阿里连气都忘了喘。
fight:1.hook: The guards watched our backs the whole way down the street.
fight:1.line: 'You don't need fists when you have *fight* in your eyes,' Grey Crow said.

finish:1.en: The broadcast tower rose dark against the neon sky. Grey Crow said reaching it would not be the *finish* — it would be the start of the hardest part. I looked at the locked gate, then at Ali, then back at the tower. Nobody moved first.
finish:1.cnHint: 灰鸦说抵达广播塔并不是____，真正困难的事还在后面。
finish:1.hook: The lock on the gate had already been cut — from the inside.
finish:1.line: 'Reaching the tower is not the *finish*,' Grey Crow said quietly.

frequently:1.en: Zero changes the courier route *frequently*, never twice the same way. Grey Crow had tracked twelve routes over six nights and still found no pattern. Tonight, standing on the wet corner, I thought I saw one. Ali said I was probably wrong. I walked anyway.
frequently:1.cnHint: 零____更换信使路线，但我觉得今晚我看出了规律——阿里不信。
frequently:1.hook: The footsteps behind me matched mine beat for beat.
frequently:1.line: 'He shifts the route *frequently* so no pattern can hold,' Grey Crow said.

invest:1.en: 'You have to *invest* time in a place before it trusts you,' Grey Crow said. He had walked this block every night for a month, buying nothing, saying little, just watching. Now the old woman at the corner stand slipped him a folded note without looking up.
invest:1.cnHint: 灰鸦说必须____时间在一个地方，它才会向你开口，街角的老人递来一张纸条。
invest:1.hook: The note had tonight's date and a single word: run.
invest:1.line: '*Invest* time here first — then the street will talk to you,' Grey Crow said.

australia:1.en: The coded broadcast crackled through my receiver. Grey Crow's voice was low: 'The shipment left *Australia* three days ago. It carries the cipher key the whole city has been hunting.' Rain hammered the street. I pressed against the wet wall, scanning rooftops for Zero's watchers.
australia:1.cnHint: 灰鸦告诉我，装有密钥的货物从____出发，已经三天了。
australia:1.hook: Somewhere above me, a red dot trembled on the wall.
australia:1.line: 'The package left *Australia* three days ago — and Zero already knows.'

authority:1.en: A black van rolled slowly past the crowd. The seal on its door meant one thing: Central *Authority*. They had power over every signal, every word spoken in Harbor City. Ali grabbed my arm. 'If they scan us here, we are finished,' she whispered. I did not argue.
authority:1.cnHint: 中央____的车出现了，阿里警告我们必须立刻离开。
authority:1.hook: The van stopped exactly in front of us.
authority:1.line: 'The Central *Authority* answers to no one — that is what makes them dangerous.'

confident:1.en: Zero stood at the far end of the bridge, coat dry despite the downpour. He looked *confident*, as if the night itself obeyed him. I had faced sharper enemies and walked away. I forced that memory forward and stepped out of the shadow to meet him.
confident:1.cnHint: 零看起来胸有成竹，但我告诉自己我也____面对过更难的对手。
confident:1.hook: He smiled, and my earpiece went suddenly dead.
confident:1.line: 'Stay *confident*, rookie — or he will smell your fear before you reach him.'

crowd:1.en: The night market was still loud, a thick *crowd* moving between stalls selling glowing food and black-market chips. I used the bodies as cover, sliding toward the drop point Grey Crow had marked on my map. Ali was somewhere behind me. I hoped she was still free.
crowd:1.cnHint: 我混入夜市的____中，悄悄向灰鸦标记的地点靠近。
crowd:1.hook: Then every stall light cut out at once.
crowd:1.line: 'Lose yourself in the *crowd* — Zero's people cannot grab you if they cannot see you.'

highly:1.en: Grey Crow's file on Zero was *highly* classified, buried under three layers of city encryption. Even reading it was a crime. But the pages I had managed to pull told me enough: Zero had dismantled four investigator teams before mine. I zipped my collar up and kept walking.
highly:1.cnHint: 关于零的档案被____保密，但我已经看到了足够多的内容。
highly:1.hook: Page five had my own name circled in red.
highly:1.line: 'That data is *highly* restricted — if you read it, you cannot pretend you did not.'

occur:1.en: It did not *occur* to me until I reached the corner that the street was too quiet. No vendors, no drones, no footsteps. In Harbor City, silence did not happen by accident. Someone had cleared this block. I turned back, but the alley behind me was already sealed.
occur:1.cnHint: 直到走到街角，我才意识到一件事——这条街____了异常。
occur:1.hook: A single overhead light flickered on, aimed at me.
occur:1.line: 'Did it not *occur* to you that an empty street in this city is a trap?'

regularly:1.en: Ali said Grey Crow *regularly* passed coded notes through the old paper-seller at the east gate. Same time, same corner, every second night. That pattern was now a weapon in Zero's hands. I checked my watch: three minutes until the next scheduled drop. I started to run.
regularly:1.cnHint: 灰鸦____通过东门的旧摊传递暗语，但这个规律现在已经暴露了。
regularly:1.hook: The paper-seller's stall was already overturned and empty.
regularly:1.line: 'He meets the courier *regularly* — Zero has had weeks to learn the schedule.'

responsible:1.en: 'Someone inside our unit is *responsible* for the leak,' Grey Crow said, not looking at me. We stood on the rain-slick overpass, city lights smearing below us. I had suspected it for days but had not spoken the thought aloud. Hearing it from him made it real and cold.
responsible:1.cnHint: 灰鸦说，内部有人要为这次泄密____，我早已有所怀疑。
responsible:1.hook: He slid a folded name across the railing toward me.
responsible:1.line: 'Someone in this unit is *responsible* for the leak — and they are still among us.'

announce:1.en: Rain hammered the street. Grey Crow pressed a stolen mic to a broadcast tower and *announced* the blackout code across every open channel. Zero's men froze on the corner. I watched from the shadow of a broken sign, pulse spiking. The whole block heard it.
announce:1.cnHint: 灰鸦通过广播塔____了停电代号，零点的人马当场愣住。
announce:1.hook: The silence after was louder than any alarm.
announce:1.line: 'I *announce* the code now — every agent on this street will hear it.'

appropriate:1.en: Ali pulled a coat from an empty guard post and threw it to me. 'It is *appropriate* for the weather and the role,' she said. I put it on without arguing. In Harbor City, borrowed identities were the only ones that kept you alive past midnight.
appropriate:1.cnHint: 阿栗认为这件外套对当前情况很____，示意我穿上它混入人群。
appropriate:1.hook: The guard post behind us was no longer empty.
appropriate:1.line: 'The disguise is *appropriate* — they will not look twice at you.'

chief:1.en: A cracked screen on the alley wall looped one face: Director Voss, Zero's *chief* operator in Harbor City. Grey Crow had told me to memorize that face. Now the screen flickered off, and someone was standing exactly where it had been.
chief:1.cnHint: 破旧屏幕上滚动播放着零点的____指挥官头像，随即画面熄灭，一个人影出现在原处。
chief:1.hook: The someone turned, and I recognized the jaw.
chief:1.line: 'Voss is the *chief* — every order in this city runs through him.'

clearly:1.en: The neon graffiti on the station wall was *clearly* a cipher. Each symbol matched a letter in the old harbor code Grey Crow had taught me. I translated it fast, hand shaking. It read: ZERO MOVES AT DAWN. Ali had to see this now.
clearly:1.cnHint: 车站墙上的霓虹涂鸦____是一段密码，我迅速译出内容，心跳加速。
clearly:1.line: 'Look — it *clearly* says Zero moves at dawn. We have no time.'

communicate:1.en: Zero had jammed every standard channel. The only way left to *communicate* with Grey Crow was the old tap-code on the water pipe that ran beneath Dock Street. I knelt in the rain, knuckles cold, and began to knock. Three short. Two long.
communicate:1.cnHint: 所有频道遭到干扰，我只能用敲击水管的方式与灰鸦____。
communicate:1.hook: A reply came — but the rhythm was wrong.
communicate:1.line: 'We *communicate* through the pipe — three short, two long, do not deviate.'

emphasis:1.en: Grey Crow's message was short: TRUST THE SIGNAL. The *emphasis* was on the last word, repeated twice in the code. Ali read it over my shoulder and went quiet. In our line of work, a repeated word was never an accident — it was a warning.
emphasis:1.cnHint: 灰鸦信息简短，其中某个词被重复强调，这种____让阿栗陷入沉默。
emphasis:1.hook: Ali's hand moved slowly toward her pocket.
emphasis:1.line: 'The *emphasis* on that word — it means someone else may have read this first.'

emphasize:1.en: Zero broadcast a single line over the stolen city feed: 'Leave now.' He did not *emphasize* it. He did not have to. Every runner on the street cleared within seconds. I stayed. Grey Crow's voice crackled in my ear: 'Good. Scared people are easier to follow.'
emphasize:1.cnHint: 零点播出冷静的警告，没有刻意____语气，街上的人却迅速散尽，只有我留了下来。
emphasize:1.hook: Then Grey Crow's signal cut to static.
emphasize:1.line: 'He did not *emphasize* it — that calm is the most dangerous kind of threat.'

england:1.en: The crate was stamped with a port seal: *England*, Dock 7, 2071. Ancient, but not forgotten. Grey Crow said the cipher system we were chasing had been smuggled out of a flooded archive in that era. Ali traced the stamp with one finger and said nothing.
england:1.cnHint: 板条箱上印有____的港口封印，灰鸦说我们追查的密码体系正源于那里。
england:1.hook: Below the stamp, someone had scratched a fresh date — tonight's.
england:1.line: 'This came from *England* decades ago — and someone just reopened the seal.'

experiment:1.en: Rain hammered the street outside the old signal tower. Grey Crow knelt beside a cracked wall panel and pointed at a row of blinking nodes. 'This block has been running an *experiment* for six months,' he said quietly. 'They fed false words into the city grid and watched which districts went dark first.' I pressed my palm to the wet concrete and felt the hidden pulse beneath.
experiment:1.cnHint: 灰鸦在废旧信号塔旁发现城市电网正在进行一场秘密的____，我感受到地面下隐藏的信号脉动。
experiment:1.hook: The pulse was not random — it spelled a name.
experiment:1.line: 'This *experiment* has been running longer than you have been alive.'

nature:1.en: Neon signs bled colour into the puddles on Fourth Street. I watched Zero move through the crowd like water — no rush, no pattern. Ali leaned close and whispered, 'That is his *nature*. He does not chase. He waits until you walk into him.' The crowd thinned. Zero had stopped, his back to a wall, eyes already on me.
nature:1.cnHint: 阿栗提醒我，零点不追人而是等待猎物自投罗网，这就是他的____，而此刻他的目光已经锁定了我。
nature:1.hook: He smiled, and my earpiece went dead.
nature:1.line: 'You cannot fight a man whose *nature* is patience.'

status:1.en: The city board glowed above the central plaza, cycling through citizen *status* codes — green for clear, amber for watched, red for flagged. My code had been amber for two days. This morning I checked and saw red. Ali grabbed my sleeve and pulled me under the overpass before the scan drone completed its turn.
status:1.cnHint: 城市公告板上显示着市民的____代码，我的代码今早变成了红色，阿栗拉着我躲到高架桥下。
status:1.hook: The drone paused directly above our hiding spot.
status:1.line: 'Your *status* just changed — we have maybe forty seconds.'

accident:1.en: Broken glass from a signal booth littered the corner of Ash Lane. Grey Crow crouched and examined the pattern. 'Not an *accident*,' he said. 'Glass falls outward when something explodes inside. This fell inward. Someone smashed it from the street to silence the broadcast.' I looked up and down the empty lane. Whoever did it was already gone.
accident:1.cnHint: 灰鸦察看碎玻璃的散落方式，断定这不是____，而是有人故意从外部砸碎信号亭来切断广播。
accident:1.hook: Then I noticed the fresh boot prints in the dust — two sets, not one.
accident:1.line: 'Trust me, this was no *accident* — look at where the glass landed.'

active:1.en: Ali pulled up a map on her wrist screen. Three nodes on the eastern grid burned white. 'Still *active*,' she said, her voice flat. 'Most stations go dark by midnight. These three never do.' I stared at the white points. They formed a triangle around the old harbour, and at the centre of that triangle sat the building Grey Crow had warned me never to enter.
active:1.cnHint: 阿栗发现东部电网有三个节点彻夜____不灭，它们围成的三角形中心正是灰鸦告诫我不要进入的大楼。
active:1.hook: As I watched, a fourth node blinked on — right where I was standing.
active:1.line: 'These three towers are still *active*, and I want to know why.'

feed:1.en: Zero had set up a small dish on the roof of a parking block overlooking the bridge. I could see it from the stairwell door. 'He is using that to *feed* false signals into the lower grid,' Grey Crow said through my earpiece. 'Every investigator chasing those signals is chasing nothing.' I counted six investigators below, all moving away from the real source.
feed:1.cnHint: 零点在停车场楼顶架设天线，向下层电网____假信号，引开了所有追查的调查员，而我看清了真正的信号来源。
feed:1.hook: The real source was the investigator standing right next to me.
feed:1.line: 'He will *feed* the grid bad data until every agent is lost in the dark.'

principle:1.en: I blocked Zero's path at the mouth of Canal Street. He stopped, hands in his coat pockets, rain plastering his hair flat. 'You work on one *principle*,' I said. 'Whoever controls the words controls the city.' He tilted his head as if I had said something polite. 'Clever,' he replied. Then the lights on the whole block cut out at once.
principle:1.cnHint: 我在运河街口拦住零点，点破了他行动所依据的核心____，他礼貌地回应，随即整条街的灯全灭了。
principle:1.hook: In the sudden dark, I heard three sets of footsteps — not two.
principle:1.line: 'Your whole operation runs on one *principle*, and I have finally found it.'

article:1.en: Grey Crow passed me a folded sheet through the gap in the fence near the waterfront. A single *article* from a banned public file — six lines of plain text, every third word replaced with a dot. 'Read the dots,' he said. 'Not the words.' I read them aloud under my breath, and the hidden sentence made my stomach drop. Zero already knew our next move.
article:1.cnHint: 灰鸦递给我一篇被禁的____，让我只读其中的省略符号而非文字，隐藏的句子令我心跳骤停。
article:1.hook: The last dot, I realised, was not a dot — it was a live tracking tag.
article:1.line: 'This *article* looks empty, but every dot in it is a word they could not print.'

immediately:1.en: The signal hit my earpiece at midnight. Grey Crow's voice was flat: 'Northeast corner, now.' I stepped out of the shelter and *immediately* read the coded graffiti on the wet wall — three slashes, one circle. Zero had already been here. The rain washed nothing away.
immediately:1.cnHint: 我在雨夜街角____看懂了墙上的暗号，意识到对手刚刚离开。
immediately:1.hook: The circle was still dripping — he had left seconds ago.
immediately:1.line: '*Immediately* after you see the mark, you move — no thinking.'

improvement:1.en: Ali crouched beside the broken signal box on Fifth Street. She had rewired it twice before, but tonight the pulses were cleaner. 'It works,' she said quietly. Grey Crow studied the readout and nodded. Every small *improvement* in our gear meant one less blind spot. Zero hated blind spots disappearing.
improvement:1.cnHint: 阿里修好了街头信号箱，我们的装备有了____，这让对手少了一个可利用的漏洞。
improvement:1.hook: Then the readout flatlined — something upstream had cut the feed.
improvement:1.line: 'Each *improvement* we make is another wall Zero cannot see through.'

afternoon:1.en: By *afternoon* the neon signs above Harbor City's market strip were already burning bright, fighting the grey sky. I walked the row twice, counting camera positions Grey Crow had marked on my map. The crowd was thick. Zero used crowds. I kept my collar up and my ears open.
afternoon:1.cnHint: ____时分，我在集市街道上数着摄像头的位置，警惕对手藏在人群中。
afternoon:1.hook: Camera seven was missing — someone had taken it down since morning.
afternoon:1.line: '*Afternoon* light is a trap — every shadow here points the wrong way.'

expand:1.en: Zero's network used to cover two city blocks. Ali pulled up the latest scan on her handheld and said nothing for a long moment. The red zones had grown. His reach could *expand* overnight, block by block, like ink dropped in water. Grey Crow traced the edge with one finger.
expand:1.cnHint: 阿里的扫描显示，对手的网络已开始____，蔓延到更多街区。
expand:1.hook: Grey Crow's finger stopped — the edge touched our safe house.
expand:1.line: 'If we let it *expand* one more block, we lose the whole east side.'

regardless:1.en: The bridge checkpoint was live. Two drones swept low, their lights cutting the rain. I had the pass Grey Crow forged, but it was old data. Ali said stay back. I crossed *regardless*, head down, steps steady. The scanner beeped once. Green. I didn't breathe until the far side.
regardless:1.cnHint: 检查站风险极高，但我____还是独自穿越了封锁线。
regardless:1.hook: Behind me, a second scanner hummed to life.
regardless:1.line: 'I crossed *regardless* — some doors only open if you don't stop.'

rid:1.en: Grey Crow met me under the rail bridge. He handed me a small device, no label, no markings. 'This will *rid* the east tower of Zero's listeners,' he said. One press, clean sweep. Simple in theory. The tower was three blocks away and every window was dark except the top floor.
rid:1.cnHint: 引路人交给我一个装置，用来____东塔里零的监听器。
rid:1.hook: One light in the top window moved — someone was already watching.
rid:1.line: 'We *rid* the tower of his ears tonight, or we go deaf tomorrow.'

dog:1.en: A thin *dog* sat at the mouth of the alley, perfectly still, watching me. Grey Crow had once said Zero used animals as markers — a living signal post. I stopped walking. Ali's voice crackled in my ear: 'Don't move it, don't touch it, just note the position.' I noted it.
dog:1.cnHint: 一只____静静坐在巷口，引路人曾说这是对手用来标记地点的活信号。
dog:1.hook: The dog turned its head east — toward our next target.
dog:1.line: 'That *dog* doesn't belong here; Zero put it there like a flag.'

busy:1.en: The intersection at Canal and Ninth was *busy* even past ten at night — food carts, noise, bodies moving in every direction. Perfect cover. I had thirty seconds to swap the data chip on the public board while no one looked. Ali counted down in my ear. Grey Crow watched the north end.
busy:1.cnHint: 运河九号路口____而嘈杂，我们趁乱在公告栏上替换了数据芯片。
busy:1.hook: Ali's countdown stopped at three — she had spotted someone she knew.
busy:1.line: 'Stay in the *busy* part — the cameras can't track a face in that crowd.'

moment:1.en: Rain hammered the street outside the transit hub. I had one *moment* — a single breath of time — to scan the crowd before Zero's signal went dark. Grey Crow pressed close behind me. 'Move,' he said. 'That window closes in three seconds.' I moved.
moment:1.cnHint: 在交通枢纽外的街道上，叙述者只有一个____来扫视人群。
moment:1.hook: The signal vanished, and someone in the crowd turned to look straight at me.
moment:1.line: 'That *moment* will not come back — so act now.'

nice:1.en: The lock on the alley gate looked cheap, but Grey Crow stopped me. 'Too *nice*,' he said. 'The edges are too clean. Standard gates rust in this rain.' He was right — the tolerances were tight, machine-fresh. Someone had swapped it out. This gate was never meant to keep people out.
nice:1.cnHint: 一扇看似普通的巷门，引路人注意到机关的____之处。
nice:1.hook: Behind the gate a soft hum rose, like something just powering on.
nice:1.line: 'The cut is too *nice* — this lock was placed here today.'

peer:1.en: Fog rolled off the bay and swallowed the lower streets. I pressed my back to a cold pillar and tried to *peer* through the white curtain. Shapes moved in the mist — one, two, three figures. Ali's voice came through my earpiece: 'Count them carefully. Zero never travels alone.'
peer:1.cnHint: 海湾的雾气笼罩街道，叙述者努力____雾中的身影。
peer:1.hook: One of the shapes stopped moving and seemed to look directly back at me.
peer:1.line: '*Peer* past the fog — tell me how many shadows you see.'

pretty:1.en: A street vendor's cart was covered in small lights and cheap charms — earrings, pins, glass beads. Every *pretty* on the cart carried a microtag. I had seen the same tags in a seized evidence box. Grey Crow bought one calmly, pocketed it, and walked on without blinking.
