announce:2.en: The ceiling speakers crackled to life. A cold voice began to *announce* the new curfew across every channel in Harbor City: no movement after dark, no signals allowed, no exceptions. Ali grabbed my arm. Grey Crow had warned us this moment would come. Now it was here.
announce:2.cnHint: 广播突然响起，当局正式____宵禁令，灰鸦早已预料到这一刻。
announce:2.hook: Someone had leaked our location before the words even finished.
announce:2.line: 'They *announce* the curfew now — we have maybe four minutes.'

appropriate:2.en: Grey Crow slid a stolen keycard across the table. 'Find something *appropriate* for the job,' he said. The archive vault held ten thousand files. I needed the one Zero had buried. Ali stood watch at the door. The rain outside hit the glass like static.
appropriate:2.cnHint: 灰鸦要我挑选____的工具进入档案库，零点把关键文件藏在了里面。
appropriate:2.hook: The card reader flashed red, then went dark entirely.
appropriate:2.line: 'Pick something *appropriate* — wrong choice and the whole vault locks.'

chief:2.en: The badge on the desk read *chief* of signals intelligence. This was Zero's office. I had thirty seconds. Ali's voice buzzed in my ear: 'Take the drive, nothing else.' A small red device sat next to an empty coffee cup, blinking once per second.
chief:2.cnHint: 我潜入了零点担任____的情报办公室，发现了一个闪烁的红色装置。
chief:2.hook: The blinking stopped — someone had just armed it remotely.
chief:2.line: 'The *chief* of signals built this trap himself — do not touch it.'

clearly:2.en: The message on the cracked screen was *clearly* meant for me. My name, my frequency, my old code phrase — all of it printed in green light. No one else in Harbor City knew that phrase. Zero knew. Ali read it over my shoulder and said nothing.
clearly:2.cnHint: 屏幕上的信息____是写给我的，零点知道一个只有我才懂的暗语。
clearly:2.hook: At the bottom of the screen, a countdown had already begun.
clearly:2.line: 'This is *clearly* a trap — and you are walking straight into it.'

communicate:2.en: Every public line in the district had gone dark. The only way left to *communicate* was the old pipe-radio Ali had salvaged from a junk stall on Level 3. Grey Crow's signal came through in short bursts. Three clicks meant danger. I counted four.
communicate:2.cnHint: 公共通讯全断了，我们只能用旧式管道收音机____，灰鸦发出的信号令人不安。
communicate:2.hook: The fourth click was not Grey Crow's rhythm at all.
communicate:2.line: 'We can only *communicate* by pipe-radio now — keep it short.'

emphasis:2.en: Grey Crow's note used bold strokes for certain letters — the *emphasis* was the message. I laid it flat under the blue lamp and read the hidden line: 'Exit is below the market, not above.' Ali had been watching the wrong floor for an hour.
emphasis:2.cnHint: 灰鸦字条上的____暗藏玄机，出口根本不在阿栗守候的那层楼。
emphasis:2.hook: Below the market, a door was already swinging open.
emphasis:2.line: 'The *emphasis* on those letters — that is the real instruction, read it.'

emphasize:2.en: Zero's broadcast looped every twenty minutes. Each time, the voice would *emphasize* a single word differently — a signal buried inside a signal. I wrote the stressed words down. They formed a street address in the old port. Ali looked at me. 'Tonight?' she asked.
emphasize:2.cnHint: 零点的广播每次都会特别____某个词，我把这些词拼在一起，得到了一个地址。
emphasize:2.hook: The address pointed to a building that burned down in 2091.
emphasize:2.line: 'They *emphasize* one word each loop — write them all down, fast.'

england:2.en: The file was stamped with a faded crest: a signal relay station once based in *England*, decommissioned in 2041 and supposedly destroyed. But the schematics in my hand were dated 2098. Someone had rebuilt it. Grey Crow had been searching for this proof for three years.
england:2.cnHint: 档案显示一座原本位于____的信号站据称已被销毁，但眼前的图纸证明它被重建了。
england:2.hook: The engineer's signature on the last page was Grey Crow's own.
england:2.line: 'This relay came from *England* — and someone brought it back to life.'

immediately:2.en: The old printer in Sub-level Nine had not worked in years. Ali dusted it off and fed in a blank card. A single line appeared: coordinates, nothing else. *Immediately* after the ink dried, the card began to dissolve — someone had laced the paper with acid. Whoever sent this message did not want it read twice.
immediately:2.cnHint: 地下九层的打印机突然打出一行坐标，纸张____开始溶解消失。
immediately:2.hook: The coordinates pointed somewhere that did not exist on any city map.
immediately:2.line: '*Immediately* after you read it,' Ali said, 'the paper eats itself.'

improvement:2.en: Grey Crow slid a cracked data chip across the wet table. 'Version three,' he said. I plugged it in. The signal was cleaner, the hidden layers easier to read — a clear *improvement* over the last build. But buried in the new code was a line I had never seen before, one that Grey Crow had not mentioned.
improvement:2.cnHint: 灰鸦交来升级版芯片，信号质量有明显____，但其中藏着一行陌生代码。
improvement:2.hook: That hidden line had only one function: to report my location.
improvement:2.line: 'The *improvement* is real,' Grey Crow said, 'but so is the price.'

afternoon:2.en: Rain had not stopped since morning. By *afternoon* a package arrived at the station — no sender, no stamp, just my name in red ink. Inside was a single photograph: Ali standing on the south bridge, eyes closed, holding a sign covered in coded text. The photo was time-stamped three hours from now.
afternoon:2.cnHint: 下午，调查站收到一个神秘包裹，里面的照片显示阿栗站在桥上，时间却是未来。
afternoon:2.hook: Someone had already seen what had not yet happened.
afternoon:2.line: 'By *afternoon*,' Ali warned earlier, 'you will understand why I went there.'

expand:2.en: Zero's signal started as a thin thread on my scanner. Over the next hour I watched it *expand* — block by block, tower by tower — until it covered the entire east grid of Harbor City. It was not a broadcast. It was a net, and every citizen with a receiver was now inside it, listening without knowing it.
expand:2.cnHint: 零点的信号在扫描仪上不断____，悄悄覆盖了整个东区网格。
expand:2.hook: My own receiver lit up, which meant I was inside the net too.
expand:2.line: 'Watch it *expand*,' Zero's voice cut in, cold and amused, 'and know you cannot stop it.'

regardless:2.en: Ali pressed the sealed drive into my hand and said nothing. The file inside named three officers — people I had trusted. I stood in the rain outside the records hall, knowing that opening it would end careers, maybe more. *Regardless*, I broke the seal. Some doors, once you see them, cannot stay closed.
regardless:2.cnHint: 阿栗交来一个封存的硬盘，里面牵涉三名官员，调查员____还是打开了它。
regardless:2.hook: The first name on the list was someone I had eaten lunch with that morning.
regardless:2.line: '*Regardless* of what it costs,' Ali said quietly, 'you needed to see this.'

rid:2.en: The graffiti tag had appeared on every tunnel wall overnight — the same eight symbols, repeating. Grey Crow told me the symbols were a purge command: whoever cracked the key could *rid* the city network of every file linked to a certain name. I checked the network log. My own file was already tagged.
rid:2.cnHint: 隧道墙上出现神秘涂鸦符号，是一条清除命令，能____城市网络中某人的所有档案。
rid:2.hook: Someone wanted me erased before I could finish the case.
rid:2.line: 'They want to *rid* the grid of you,' Grey Crow said, 'like you never existed.'

intelligence:2.en: Grey Crow slid a worn data chip across the wet table. 'Every move Zero makes is logged here,' he said quietly. The raw *intelligence* was staggering — locations, timestamps, encrypted names. I pressed the chip into my palm. Outside, neon signs bled red into the rain.
intelligence:2.cnHint: 灰鸦交给我一块芯片，里面存满了关于零点的____。
intelligence:2.hook: One name on the list made my blood go cold.
intelligence:2.line: 'This *intelligence* cost three good people their freedom — use it well.'

uk:2.en: A fragment of old broadcast crackled through my earpiece: coordinates tagged *UK*, a pre-collapse server node that Zero had reactivated deep inside Harbor City's east grid. Ali traced the signal to a rusted relay tower. The node was live. Someone was listening.
uk:2.cnHint: 阿栗追踪到一个信号，源头标注着____，那是一个被重新激活的旧服务器节点。
uk:2.hook: The signal carried a voice we both recognized.
uk:2.line: 'That *UK* node should have gone dark eighty years ago — why is it breathing again?'

user:2.en: The terminal blinked one word: ACCESS DENIED. I tried Grey Crow's old pass-key. Still nothing. Then Ali whispered, 'Check the *user* log.' A single account had been active four minutes ago — handle: Z3R0. My fingers froze above the keys.
user:2.cnHint: 阿栗让我查看终端的____记录，结果发现了一个熟悉的账号。
user:2.hook: The account was still logged in — from inside this building.
user:2.line: 'Every *user* on this system is being watched — including whoever just read that file.'

park:2.en: Ali found the dead drop behind a cracked bench in Signal *Park*, the strip of dead grass between two server towers. A folded card lay under the armrest. On it: six digits and a frequency. Grey Crow had told me to look here. I had not told anyone else.
park:2.cnHint: 阿栗在____里的一条长椅下找到了一张写有密码的纸条。
park:2.hook: The ink on the card was still damp.
park:2.line: 'Meet me at the east gate of *Park* Nine when the clock tower goes silent.'

reward:2.en: Zero's broadcast cut through every channel at midnight: a *reward* for whoever handed over my ID number — enough credits to vanish from Harbor City forever. I heard it through three walls. Ali squeezed my arm once, said nothing. The offer expired at dawn.
reward:2.cnHint: 零点在广播中宣布，谁能举报我就能获得____。
reward:2.hook: By morning, someone had already made the call.
reward:2.line: 'No *reward* is worth what Zero will do to the person who collects it.'

credit:2.en: The locked archive opened only for accounts with a clearance *credit* above nine hundred. Mine sat at four hundred. Grey Crow's old ID, borrowed for thirty seconds, read nine sixty. The files copied fast. I deleted the access trail and stepped back into the dark corridor.
credit:2.cnHint: 我借用灰鸦的账户____值解锁了那份机密档案。
credit:2.hook: The system had already flagged the login as irregular.
credit:2.line: 'Your *credit* score in this network is your life — guard it like one.'

progress:2.en: Each decoded layer brought me closer, yet Zero seemed to *progress* faster — sealing exits, burning nodes, rewriting the city's signal map ahead of me. Ali spread the data on the floor. 'We are losing ground,' she said flatly. Grey Crow's last message had warned us of exactly this.
progress:2.cnHint: 零点不断____，一步步封锁我们的追查路线。
progress:2.hook: The next node on our map had just gone dark.
progress:2.line: 'If we don't *progress* past this block in ten minutes, the whole trail goes cold.'

snack:2.en: Ali pushed a foil packet across the table — a dry *snack*, the kind sold at every corner stall in the lower grid. Pressed inside the wrapper was a micro-strip of film. Grey Crow's handwriting covered it edge to edge. I read it twice, then chewed the strip into nothing.
snack:2.cnHint: 阿栗递给我一包____，里面藏着灰鸦手写的情报胶片。
snack:2.hook: The last line on the strip named someone I trusted completely.
snack:2.line: 'Eat your *snack* — and don't let anyone see what comes out of the wrapper.'

male:2.en: The hidden signal led me to a back-street clinic. A *male* voice on the broadcast repeated the same four numbers, low and steady. Ali pressed close and whispered that the voice belonged to someone Grey Crow had warned us about. The door at the end of the corridor was already open.
male:2.cnHint: 调查员在诊所收听到一段____声音的加密广播，阿栗认出了说话者的身份。
male:2.hook: Behind that open door, something blinked in the dark.
male:2.line: 'That *male* voice — I have heard it before, in a coded file Grey Crow buried.'

fish:2.en: Sealed inside a cold-storage unit, wrapped in foil, was a single dried *fish*. Ali cut it open with a blade. Inside the flesh was a strip of encoded film, thin as paper. Grey Crow had promised the next clue would hide in plain sight. He was right.
fish:2.cnHint: 阿栗在冷藏室的一条____体内发现了藏匿的加密胶片。
fish:2.hook: The film showed a face neither of us had expected to see.
fish:2.line: 'The *fish* was the drop point — whoever left it knew we were coming.'

fashion:2.en: Zero had left the message in the old *fashion*: graffiti scratched into a vent cover, each letter shifted by three. I decoded it in under a minute. It read: MEET THE ROOF. Ali checked the time. We had four minutes left.
fashion:2.cnHint: 零点用一种旧式____在通风口留下加密信息，调查员迅速破译了它。
fashion:2.hook: The roof access light had already turned green.
fashion:2.line: 'Zero still works in the old *fashion* — always graffiti, always shifted code.'

weather:2.en: The *weather* report broadcast at midnight was not about rain. Each degree reading was a grid coordinate. I mapped them fast and the pattern pointed to Pier Nine. Ali grabbed her coat. Grey Crow had told us once: the city talks, if you know which channel to tune.
weather:2.cnHint: 调查员发现深夜____预报中隐藏着通往九号码头的坐标信息。
weather:2.hook: Pier Nine had been closed since the blackout three years ago.
weather:2.line: 'Listen — tonight the *weather* report is the only map we have got.'

device:2.en: Grey Crow had hidden a small *device* behind the vending unit in the east tunnel — no larger than a coin, but it was reading every signal that passed through the wall. I pulled it free and the data began to stream. Ali went pale when she saw the source address.
device:2.cnHint: 灰鸦在隧道中藏了一个____，它记录了穿墙而过的所有加密信号。
device:2.hook: The source address pointed directly to our own bureau.
device:2.line: 'This *device* has been here for weeks — someone planned this long before us.'

farm:2.en: The coordinates decoded to an address outside the city grid: an old vertical *farm*, thirty floors of dark soil and dead lights. Zero had chosen it well — no cameras, no foot traffic, only the hum of broken pipes. Ali and I climbed in through a broken panel on level two.
farm:2.cnHint: 解密坐标指向城郊一座废弃的____，零点将秘密藏匿于此。
farm:2.hook: On level three, a single grow-light flickered on.
farm:2.line: 'An old *farm* — no cameras, no guards. Zero always picks the forgotten places.'

drug:2.en: The package Grey Crow left was tagged with a biohazard seal, but the contents were not medical. Inside was a data chip encoded with a banned *drug* formula — not for use, but as a key. Whoever built this lock was creative, and cruel. Ali said nothing. She just stared at the chip.
drug:2.cnHint: 灰鸦留下的包裹里藏着一枚以违禁____配方加密的芯片，它是打开某扇门的钥匙。
drug:2.hook: The lock it opened was inside the city archive.
drug:2.line: 'The *drug* formula is not the threat — it is just the password. Think bigger.'

heat:2.en: The server room at sub-level four was running far too hot. The *heat* hit us the moment the door slid open — someone had been running a heavy decode job for hours. Ali checked the logs. The last command had finished forty seconds before we arrived. We had just missed them.
heat:2.cnHint: 调查员发现地下服务器室异常____，有人刚刚完成了一次大规模解密后迅速逃离。
heat:2.hook: The decoded file was still open on the screen.
heat:2.line: 'Feel that *heat* — whoever was here left in a hurry and did not wipe the screen.'

extreme:2.en: The signal hit me like cold water. Buried inside a public broadcast was a hidden message, and its *extreme* urgency was clear — three short pulses, then silence. Grey Crow had taught me that pattern. It meant the operation had changed. I checked my tracker. The source was two blocks north, moving fast.
extreme:2.cnHint: 广播里藏着一条紧急信号，叙述者意识到行动计划已经改变，信号的____程度令人震惊。
extreme:2.hook: The tracker blinked once — then went dark.
extreme:2.line: 'The *extreme* signal means we move now, no waiting.'

style:2.en: The graffiti on the wet wall was not random. Each letter was cut in a sharp, angular *style* I had seen once before — in Zero's old case files. Ali crouched beside me, reading it aloud in a low voice. The message was short. It named a time. It named a place. It named me.
style:2.cnHint: 墙上的涂鸦用一种特殊的____写成，叙述者认出了那是对手零点的笔迹。
style:2.hook: The ink was still wet — written less than ten minutes ago.
style:2.line: 'That *style* of writing belongs to only one person in Harbor City.'

color:2.en: Ali pressed the small card into my hand without a word. Under the blue neon light I saw it clearly — the *color* of the ink was not black but deep red, a code only Grey Crow used. My fingers went cold. This card had not come from Grey Crow. Someone was copying the signal.
color:2.cnHint: 阿栗交给叙述者一张卡片，卡片上墨水的____是一种只有引路人才会用的暗号。
color:2.hook: I looked up — Ali was already gone.
color:2.line: 'The *color* of the ink is the first thing you check — always.'

meeting:2.en: The encrypted file listed only one event: a *meeting* at midnight, sub-level four of the old port tower. No names, no agenda — just a set of coordinates and a single warning word I could not yet decode. Grey Crow had circled it twice in red. I had forty minutes to get there.
meeting:2.cnHint: 一份加密文件记录了一场深夜____，叙述者只有40分钟赶到那个地点。
meeting:2.hook: The warning word began to pulse — it was a live signal.
meeting:2.line: 'This *meeting* was set before either of us arrived in Harbor City.'

volunteer:2.en: The name on the list stopped me cold: *volunteer*, written in plain text among rows of encrypted handles. It was not a job title. In Grey Crow's code system, it meant someone had stepped forward without being asked — someone willing to carry the risk alone. I knew only one person that bold. Ali.
volunteer:2.cnHint: 一份名单上出现了"____"这个词，叙述者根据引路人的密码系统，推断出那个主动承担风险的人是阿栗。
volunteer:2.hook: Ali's locator signal had been off for the last six hours.
volunteer:2.line: 'A *volunteer* in our network means someone chose danger on purpose.'

deliver:2.en: The drone dropped a sealed case at my feet and rose back into the rain without a sound. Inside was a data chip and a short note: 'Zero will *deliver* the final code at dawn — intercept it or the city network falls.' The handwriting was Grey Crow's, but the ink smelled wrong. A trap, or a warning?
deliver:2.cnHint: 一架无人机送来一个密封箱子，纸条上说对手零点将在黎明____最终代码，叙述者必须拦截。
deliver:2.hook: The chip was already warm — someone had accessed it before me.
deliver:2.line: 'If Zero gets to *deliver* that code, we lose every channel in the city.'

engineering:2.en: The hidden room under the port was full of equipment I barely understood. Grey Crow swept a light across the racks and said one word: *engineering*. Not simple hacking — this was a full rebuild of the city's language grid, designed to erase certain words from every live broadcast forever. Someone had been planning this for years.
engineering:2.cnHint: 地下密室里摆满了设备，引路人告诉叙述者，这是一项针对全城语言系统的____工程，策划已久。
engineering:2.hook: One rack was still running — its screen showed my name.
engineering:2.line: 'This level of *engineering* means we are already too late to stop the build.'

tiny:2.en: I almost missed it. Taped to the back of a pipe in the corner of the room was a *tiny* chip, no bigger than my thumbnail. Ali had told me once that the smallest carries the most. I peeled it free, held it to the light. A single line of text glowed on its surface — coordinates I already knew by heart.
tiny:2.cnHint: 叙述者在角落里发现了一枚____的芯片，上面的文字让他大吃一惊。
tiny:2.hook: The coordinates pointed directly to Grey Crow's safe house.
tiny:2.line: 'A *tiny* chip like this can carry enough data to shut down the whole grid.'

retire:2.en: The old data tower stood at the edge of Harbor City's lower grid. Ali pointed to a rusted door. 'Grey Crow used to work here,' she said quietly. 'Before he chose to *retire* from the agency and disappear into the city's noise.' A faint signal still pulsed from inside — low, coded, alive.
retire:2.cnHint: 阿栗告诉我，灰鸦选择____离开情报机构，但这栋废弃大楼里似乎仍有信号在跳动。
retire:2.hook: The signal was not old. Someone had sent it ten minutes ago.
retire:2.line: 'I *retired* so they would stop looking — but they never did.'

sea:2.en: A forgotten weather map glowed on the cracked wall of sub-level nine. It showed Harbor City before the flood years — open land, no towers, just a wide *sea* pressing against the coast. Ali traced its edge with one finger. Zero had left this map here on purpose. Every border was marked with a tiny cipher.
sea:2.cnHint: 地下九层的旧地图显示着____曾经的模样，零点故意将它留在此处，地图边界藏着密码。
sea:2.hook: The cipher on the southern shore matched the code in my head.
sea:2.line: 'The *sea* swallowed the old city — and Zero wants to finish the job.'

town:2.en: Grey Crow's file listed a birth record from a small *town* two hundred kilometers inland, a place the city's network had never fully reached. Ali flagged the entry — the town's name was a banned word in Harbor City's public feed, scrubbed clean six years ago. Whatever happened there, someone wanted it erased.
town:2.cnHint: 灰鸦的档案显示他来自一个内陆小____，而这个地名已被列为禁词，从公开网络中彻底抹去。
town:2.hook: The scrubbing date matched the night Grey Crow first contacted me.
town:2.line: 'That *town* is why Zero has been hunting me since day one.'

gap:2.en: The encrypted broadcast ran every hour, but I noticed a *gap* — eleven seconds of silence between the fourth and fifth signal burst. No accident. Ali confirmed it: that gap was a carrier channel, too short for standard scanners to catch. Someone was hiding a second message inside the quiet.
gap:2.cnHint: 我发现加密广播中存在一段____，阿栗确认这段沉默本身就是隐藏第二条信息的载波通道。
gap:2.hook: The hidden message inside the gap was addressed to my name.
gap:2.line: 'Find the *gap*, and you find what Zero does not want heard.'

generation:2.en: The server room beneath the market held drives stacked floor to ceiling. Ali read the labels — each one a *generation* of Harbor City's language filter, version after version, each one trained to catch more words, silence more voices. The oldest drive was cracked open. Something had been copied out of it long ago.
generation:2.cnHint: 地下服务器室里存放着Harbor City语言过滤器的每一____版本，最旧的那块硬盘已被人复制过数据。
generation:2.hook: Grey Crow's ID tag was scratched into the side of that oldest drive.
generation:2.line: 'Every *generation* of the filter is in here — and every lie it was built on.'

guide:2.en: Folded inside the lining of an old coat left in locker seven was a small printed card. On one side, a street map of the lower grid. On the other, two words: FOLLOW SOUND. It was a *guide* — hand-drawn, deliberate, meant for exactly one person. The locker number matched a code Ali had pulled that morning.
guide:2.cnHint: 储物柜七号的旧外套夹层里藏着一张手绘____，正面是地图，背面写着两个字：跟着声音走。
guide:2.hook: The map led directly under Zero's known safe house.
guide:2.line: 'This *guide* was drawn for you — Grey Crow knew you were coming.'

household:2.en: The safe house looked like any ordinary *household* from the outside — dim windows, a pot of dead plants, a worn mat at the door. But every object inside was a node: the lamp a transmitter, the clock a frequency lock, the mat a pressure sensor linked to a silent alarm. Ali had lived here once. She would not say when.
household:2.cnHint: 这间普通____外表掩盖着精密的信号网络，每件家具都是节点，阿栗曾在此居住，但不愿说明时间。
household:2.hook: The pressure mat logged a visitor at three in the morning — last night.
household:2.line: 'It looks like a normal *household* — that is exactly why Zero chose it.'

luxury:2.en: Zero's last known location was a high tower on the north shore, the kind of address that meant money and silence both. *Luxury* was the cover — polished floors, filtered air, staff who asked no questions. But Grey Crow had told me once: the higher the floor, the easier to broadcast without walls in the way.
luxury:2.cnHint: 零点藏身于北岸高档____公寓，灰鸦曾提醒我：楼层越高，无线电广播越畅通无阻。
luxury:2.hook: A broadcast was live right now, coming from the top floor.
luxury:2.line: '*Luxury* is just a signal tower with better furniture,' Grey Crow had said.

analysis:2.en: The data chip felt cold in my palm. Ali had pulled it from the old server before it burned. I ran a quick *analysis* of the signal patterns inside — seven layers of code, each one hiding a different name. Six names I knew. The seventh made my hands shake.
analysis:2.cnHint: 我对芯片里的信号做了____，发现了一个令人震惊的名字。
analysis:2.line: 'My *analysis* shows someone inside this building sent the kill order.'

application:2.en: Grey Crow slid a folded paper across the wet table. It looked like a school *application* form — name, age, district. But every third letter, read in order, spelled out coordinates. Harbor City Academy. Sub-level four. Tonight.
application:2.cnHint: 那份看似普通的____表格里，藏着一串秘密坐标。
application:2.hook: Sub-level four did not appear on any city map.
application:2.line: 'Fill out the *application* — and read every third letter carefully.'

living:2.en: The safe house was a narrow room above a noodle shop. Ali looked around at the cracked walls and dim light. 'This is how we are *living* now?' she said quietly. I did not answer. On the floor, a fresh message had been burned into the boards: ZERO KNOWS.
living:2.cnHint: 我们藏身在一间破旧的小屋里，地板上却出现了一行烧焦的____警告。
living:2.hook: The burned words were still warm.
living:2.line: '*Living* like this means someone already found our last safe house.'

proposal:2.en: Zero's *proposal* arrived as graffiti on the east wall of Harbor City Station — white letters on black tile, clean and cold: trade the chip for safe passage, midnight, the old bridge. Grey Crow read it twice and said nothing. Silence from Grey Crow was never good.
proposal:2.cnHint: 零点把他的____写成涂鸦，留在了车站的墙上，条件冷酷而清晰。
proposal:2.hook: Grey Crow's silence meant the offer was a trap.
proposal:2.line: 'Zero's *proposal* looks fair — that is exactly why we should not trust it.'

relevant:2.en: I spread every file across the floor of the archive room. Most were old noise — city permits, weather logs, dead signals. Then Ali pointed at a single line buried on page nine. 'That part is *relevant*,' she said. It was a transfer order, signed the night the signal tower went dark.
relevant:2.cnHint: 阿栗在一堆档案中发现了一条____的关键线索——一份转移命令。
relevant:2.hook: The signature on the order belonged to someone we thought was dead.
relevant:2.line: 'Only one line in this whole file is *relevant* — and it names Grey Crow.'

senior:2.en: The man waiting at the archive desk was old, calm, and said very little. Ali told me he was a *senior* officer from the first signal wars — retired, or so the records claimed. He pushed a sealed envelope toward me without looking up. Inside was a single key and no note.
senior:2.cnHint: 一位____官员递给我一个密封信封，里面只有一把钥匙，没有任何说明。
senior:2.hook: The key was cut for a lock that no longer existed — officially.
senior:2.line: 'As a *senior* in this unit, I have seen this key before. It opens something buried.'

table:2.en: The map was not on any screen. It was carved into the underside of the *table* in room nine of the old district office — thin lines, tiny numbers, a grid of tunnels beneath Harbor City. Ali ran her fingers along the grooves. Someone had hidden this years ago and never came back for it.
table:2.cnHint: 房间里那张____的底面刻着一幅地下隧道地图，等待多年无人取走。
table:2.hook: One tunnel on the map led directly under Zero's tower.
table:2.line: 'Check under the *table* — people always hide what matters where no one looks.'

campus:2.en: The dead drop was set inside the old university *campus* on the north edge of the city — abandoned since the signal riots, gates rusted shut, every wall covered in coded tags. I found the message tucked behind a broken lecture board. Four words. Grey Crow had been here first.
campus:2.cnHint: 我在废弃的____里找到了灰鸦留下的秘密纸条，只有四个词。
campus:2.hook: The four words told me I had been following the wrong person all along.
campus:2.line: 'Meet me on *campus* at the north gate — and come alone, or the message burns.'

destroy:2.en: The archive room smelled of burnt plastic. Grey Crow pointed at the server rack — every drive wiped, every cable cut. Someone had worked fast. 'They came to *destroy* the evidence,' he said, voice flat. My flashlight swept the dark corners. One small drive lay under a dead terminal, overlooked.
destroy:2.cnHint: 灰鸦发现档案室的服务器被人蓄意____，但角落里还藏着一块遗漏的硬盘。
destroy:2.hook: That single drive held everything they tried to erase.
destroy:2.line: 'They came to *destroy* the evidence before dawn.'

drop:2.en: Ali passed me a sealed glass tube. Inside, one *drop* of deep-blue liquid caught the light like a cold star. 'Lab found it on the keyboard,' she whispered. 'Whatever it is, it does not belong to any registered chemical on record.' The corridor outside fell suddenly silent.
drop:2.cnHint: 阿栗交给我一支密封试管，里面只有一____奇怪的蓝色液体。
drop:2.hook: One drop — and someone had already died for it.
drop:2.line: 'Just one *drop*, but the lab has never seen it before.'

efficiency:2.en: The hacked transit board above Gate Nine scrolled a hidden message in plain sight. Grey Crow read it aloud, slow: 'Maximum *efficiency* — remove all noise.' I felt cold. In Zero's code, noise meant people. The board reset, and the words were gone, as if they had never been there.
efficiency:2.cnHint: 黑客在公告屏上藏了一条暗语，其中"____"二字让我不寒而栗。
efficiency:2.hook: Zero's idea of noise was not static — it was us.
efficiency:2.line: 'Maximum *efficiency* — that means they plan to cut us out.'

italian:2.en: The folded note tucked inside the cracked terminal was written in neat, old-fashioned script — *Italian*, Grey Crow said, squinting. He translated three words aloud: 'the eye watches.' Ali checked the security feed. Camera seven, the one everyone assumed was broken, had been recording for six days straight.
italian:2.cnHint: 藏在终端机里的纸条用____语写成，翻译出来只有三个字让人背脊发凉。
italian:2.hook: Six days of footage — and we were in every frame.
italian:2.line: 'It is written in *Italian* — someone wanted only us to find it.'

newspaper:2.en: A single *newspaper* lay open on the wet floor of the abandoned print shop, dated three weeks ahead. The headline read: HARBOR CITY GOES DARK — FINAL BROADCAST. Ali stared at it. 'This is not old stock,' she said. 'The ink is fresh.' My hands would not stop shaking.
newspaper:2.cnHint: 一张____出现在废弃印刷厂里，头版标题写的却是三周后的日期。
newspaper:2.hook: Fresh ink on a future date — someone had already planned the ending.
newspaper:2.line: 'This *newspaper* is dated three weeks from today — read the headline.'

piece:2.en: Grey Crow laid six memory chips on the table like a broken puzzle. 'Each *piece* holds one fragment of the signal,' he said. 'Alone they mean nothing.' Ali began to sort them by the faint serial marks along each edge. Outside, the rain hammered the roof and something moved in the alley.
piece:2.cnHint: 灰鸦把六块芯片摆上桌，说明每一____单独都毫无意义。
piece:2.hook: Before Ali could finish sorting, the alley door swung open.
piece:2.line: 'Each *piece* alone is noise — together they are the signal.'

target:2.en: The red dot on the city map had no street name, no building code — just a pin. 'That is Zero's next *target*,' Grey Crow said, circling it in grease pencil. I cross-checked the grid. The pin sat dead-centre on the city's main relay tower. If it fell, every signal in Harbor City would die.
target:2.cnHint: 地图上的红点标出了零点的下一个____，那是全城信号的核心所在。
target:2.hook: We had four hours before Zero's window opened.
target:2.line: 'The relay tower is the real *target* — Zero planned this from the start.'

actual:2.en: The file said the blackout was a drill. Grey Crow shook his head. 'The *actual* plan,' he said, sliding a second document across the desk, 'is buried in the appendix.' I read it twice. The drill was a cover. While every investigator watched the sky, Zero's team would move underground, unseen.
actual:2.cnHint: 官方文件说停电只是演习，但灰鸦揭示了____的计划截然不同。
actual:2.hook: By the time anyone looked underground, it would be too late.
actual:2.line: 'Forget the drill — the *actual* plan is hidden in the last page.'

pursue:2.en: The rooftop broadcast cut out at midnight. Grey Crow's voice crackled in my earpiece: 'Zero is moving east — *pursue* him or lose the signal forever.' I ran hard across wet tiles, wind sharp as broken glass, each step taking me deeper into the dark grid of Harbor City.
pursue:2.cnHint: 引路人命令我____零点，否则将永远失去那个信号。
pursue:2.hook: The signal blinked once, then vanished into the storm.
pursue:2.line: '*Pursue* him now — every second you wait, he rewrites the code.'

site:2.en: Ali pulled up a blurred map on her cracked screen. 'The drop is at the old relay tower — that *site* has been dead for thirty years, but someone just powered it back on.' Cold rain tapped the window. We grabbed our gear and stepped into the neon-stained dark.
site:2.cnHint: 阿栗发现那个____突然重新通电，藏着某种秘密。
site:2.hook: A single light blinked on inside the tower — we were expected.
site:2.line: 'That *site* went dark in 2069 — someone wants us to go there.'

absorb:2.en: The stolen chip was small, but its data could *absorb* every coded message broadcast across Harbor City in the last decade. Grey Crow held it up to the pale light. 'This is why Zero killed for it,' he said quietly. Outside, sirens began to rise.
absorb:2.cnHint: 那枚芯片能____整个城市十年来的加密信息，代价极大。
absorb:2.hook: Grey Crow's hand trembled — he had read something he wished he hadn't.
absorb:2.line: 'It can *absorb* a decade of secrets — and Zero knows we have it.'

advance:2.en: Zero sent the message three hours before the raid — a clear *advance* warning to someone inside our unit. Ali stared at the timestamp, her jaw tight. 'There is a leak,' she said. The lights in the safe house flickered once and went black.
advance:2.cnHint: 零点提前发出的____警告说明我们内部出现了叛徒。
advance:2.hook: Ali's eyes landed on the one person still holding a lit screen.
advance:2.line: 'An *advance* message means someone here is feeding him our plans.'

capable:2.en: The lock on the archive vault was rated against any known tool. Grey Crow studied it, then looked at me. 'Zero is *capable* of cracking this in under a minute — which means he has already been inside.' The dust on the floor told the rest of the story.
capable:2.cnHint: 灰鸦断定零点____破解这把锁，而且已经动过手了。
capable:2.hook: One file was missing — the only file that could clear my name.
capable:2.line: 'He is *capable* of this and worse — check what is already gone.'

dollar:2.en: The ransom note demanded one *dollar* — a single, physical coin, minted in 2031. Ali laughed, but her eyes did not. 'It is not about the money,' she said. 'It is a code. Someone is telling us exactly where to meet, and exactly how much time we have left.'
dollar:2.cnHint: 勒索信只要一枚____，阿栗意识到这其实是一条暗语。
dollar:2.hook: The coin in my pocket was minted in 2031 — I had carried it for years.
dollar:2.line: 'One *dollar*, hand-delivered — this is a message, not a price.'

double:2.en: The evidence file had been copied — a *double* of every record sat on a server we did not control. Grey Crow's face went still. 'Zero planned this from the start,' he said. 'Whatever we find tonight, he already knows.' The city hummed outside, indifferent and vast.
double:2.cnHint: 所有证据文件都有一份____，零点早就掌握了我们的一切。
double:2.hook: Grey Crow deleted our copy — and the other one updated instantly.
double:2.line: 'A *double* of every file — he has watched us from the beginning.'

federal:2.en: The signal led to a sealed basement beneath the old *federal* records hall — a building no local officer could legally enter. Ali handed me a cold badge. 'Grey Crow pulled strings,' she said. 'We have one hour before they notice it is fake.' The door groaned open.
federal:2.cnHint: 线索指向那栋____档案大楼的地下室，我们只有一小时假冒身份。
federal:2.hook: Inside, every shelf was empty — except for one folder marked with my name.
federal:2.line: 'The *federal* seal buys us one hour — do not waste a single second.'

campaign:2.en: Deep in the Archive Tower, I found a cracked data-chip. Grey Crow said it mapped a secret *campaign* to erase every coded dialect from Harbor City — block by block, district by district. The map was dated tomorrow. Ali pressed her back against the cold wall and said nothing.
campaign:2.cnHint: 我在档案塔里发现了一块破损芯片，记录着一场针对港城方言的秘密____计划。
campaign:2.hook: Tomorrow's date meant the first move had already been made.
campaign:2.line: 'This *campaign* started long before they told us,' Grey Crow said.

hurt:2.en: The message was written in red on the sub-level wall: TRUTH DOES NOT *HURT* — SILENCE DOES. Ali photographed it fast. Zero had left it, I was sure. It was not a warning. It was a confession, and confessions only appear when someone expects to disappear.
hurt:2.cnHint: 地下通道的墙上出现了一条红色留言，暗示沉默才是真正的____。
hurt:2.hook: Ali's hand shook as she lowered the camera.
hurt:2.line: 'Silence *hurts* more than any word ever could,' Zero had written.

initiative:2.en: No one told me to go to the Signal Market alone. I took the *initiative*, following a faint pulse code only I could hear. Between two broken stalls I found a folded paper — coordinates, no name. Grey Crow had warned me: those who move first in Harbor City rarely move twice.
initiative:2.cnHint: 没人命令我独自行动，我凭借自己的____来到信号市场，找到了一张神秘字条。
initiative:2.hook: The coordinates pointed directly beneath the Investigator's own office.
initiative:2.line: 'Taking *initiative* here is either brave or foolish,' Ali said quietly.

jump:2.en: The data-stream flickered. I watched the numbers *jump* — a sudden spike at exactly noon, same pattern three days running. Ali said it was noise. Grey Crow said noise does not repeat. Someone was sending a pulse from inside the Central Grid, and they wanted us to notice.
jump:2.cnHint: 数据流中出现异常____，三天来每天正午准时出现同一规律。
jump:2.hook: On the fourth day, the signal spelled out my name.
jump:2.line: 'Watch the numbers *jump* — that is not random,' Grey Crow said.

lunch:2.en: The package arrived during *lunch* — a plain box slid under the door of the safe room while Ali and I ate in silence. Inside: one photograph, no note. It showed the three of us together at a place we had never been. Zero was proving something cold and simple: he was always closer than we thought.
lunch:2.cnHint: 午____时间，一个神秘包裹被塞进门缝，里面是一张我们从未去过的地方的合照。
lunch:2.hook: The photograph was dated two days from now.
lunch:2.line: 'Someone sent this during *lunch* — they know our schedule,' Ali said.

necessarily:2.en: Grey Crow spread the decoded files on the floor. 'A hidden signal does not *necessarily* mean an enemy,' he said. But the file names matched every move I had made since arriving in Harbor City. I stared at the list. Ally or enemy, someone had been writing my story before I lived it.
necessarily:2.cnHint: 格雷·克劳提醒我，发现隐藏信号并不____意味着敌人的存在，但证据让人不安。
necessarily:2.hook: The last file name was simply: ENDING.
necessarily:2.line: 'Evidence does not *necessarily* tell the whole truth,' Grey Crow said.

psychologist:2.en: Tucked behind a loose tile in the East Archive was a hand-written card: DR. VENN — *PSYCHOLOGIST*, GRID SECTOR 7. Ali did not recognise the name. Grey Crow went still. The card was old, but the ink on the back was fresh: a single word — REMEMBER — in Zero's exact handwriting.
psychologist:2.cnHint: 一张藏在瓷砖后的名片上写着一位____的姓名，背面是零用新墨水写下的神秘字样。
psychologist:2.hook: Grey Crow's silence lasted exactly too long.
psychologist:2.line: 'A *psychologist* who works for the Grid knows every weak point,' Zero had written.

disadvantage:2.en: The signal came from a blind spot beneath the old bridge. Every investigator knew this district: no cover, three open sight lines, rain cutting visibility to ten metres. Fighting here put us at a clear *disadvantage*. Yet Grey Crow had chosen it. That meant the location was not a trap — it was a message.
disadvantage:2.cnHint: 我意识到在这个地点行动对我们来说是一种____，但引路人选择它自有深意。
disadvantage:2.hook: Grey Crow never chose a bad position by accident.
disadvantage:2.line: 'Every *disadvantage* hides the shape of their plan,' Grey Crow said.

discuss:2.en: Ali slid a folded card across the wet table. On it, three words: MEET. ROOFTOP. MIDNIGHT. 'Zero left this at the drop point,' she said. I turned the card over. Nothing. 'We need to *discuss* what Zero wants before we walk into that meeting,' I told her. She nodded once, eyes already moving to the door.
discuss:2.cnHint: 阿栗带来了零点留下的纸条，我们必须先____它再赴约。
discuss:2.hook: But the rooftop light was already blinking — someone was there now.
discuss:2.line: 'We *discuss* this fast — midnight is three hours away,' Ali said.

psychological:2.en: The broadcast cut in at 03:00, same as the four nights before. A voice. No words — only a low tone that pressed behind my eyes. Grey Crow called it *psychological* noise: designed not to inform but to wear a listener down, one sleepless hour at a time. Zero was not sending a message. Zero was sending exhaustion.
psychological:2.cnHint: 零点播放的神秘声音是一种____手段，目的是让我们精疲力竭。
psychological:2.hook: On the fifth morning I found I could no longer trust my own memory.
psychological:2.line: 'It is pure *psychological* pressure — Zero wants you too tired to think,' Grey Crow said.

request:2.en: A sealed envelope sat in the evidence locker, tagged but unopened. Inside: one line of type and a single frequency code. It was a *request* — formal, almost polite — asking me to transmit my route plan for the next operation. Signed with Zero's mark. I set it down carefully. Someone inside our unit had placed it there.
request:2.cnHint: 证物柜里有一封信，是零点发来的____，而且是内部人放进去的。
request:2.hook: Only four people knew that locker's code.
request:2.line: 'A *request* this polite from Zero means a threat underneath it,' Ali said.

symptom:2.en: Grey Crow spread the case files across the floor of the safe room. Seven incidents. Different districts, different methods. 'Taken alone, each one looks minor,' he said. 'But each is a *symptom* of the same deeper fault — someone is testing the city's defences, mapping the gaps.' I stared at the pattern. The final gap was exactly where we stood.
symptom:2.cnHint: 七起事件分散各处，引路人说每一件都是同一隐患的____。
symptom:2.hook: The gap in the map pointed straight at our safe room.
symptom:2.line: 'One *symptom* alone means nothing — together they name the disease,' Grey Crow said.

upon:2.en: Ali found the drive taped *upon* the underside of the bench in the transit hub — exactly where the anonymous tip had said. She did not touch it. We had been given the location too easily. I photographed it from four angles and walked away. Free information in Harbor City always cost something; we just had not found the price yet.
upon:2.cnHint: 阿栗在长椅____发现了那个数据盘，但来得太容易让人起疑。
upon:2.hook: By the time we reached the exit, every screen in the hub went dark.
upon:2.line: 'Someone placed it *upon* that bench and then watched us find it,' I said.

argument:2.en: Zero's transmission contained no threat, no demand — only a single, cold *argument*: that the city's encrypted grid would collapse in seventy-two hours, and that only Zero held the restore key. The logic was clean. The evidence attached was real. I hated that I could not find a flaw. Grey Crow was already on his feet, coat on.
argument:2.cnHint: 零点发来的信息不是威胁，而是一个冷静的____，声称掌握着城市命运。
argument:2.hook: Grey Crow's silence told me he could not find a flaw either.
argument:2.line: 'That *argument* is too clean — someone built it to look unbreakable,' Grey Crow said.

crisis:2.en: The alert arrived as three short pulses on my wrist band: the city-wide code for a communication *crisis*. Every encrypted channel was degrading at once. Ali read the numbers on her screen and went pale. 'We have maybe forty minutes before the whole network goes silent,' she said. Forty minutes to find Zero. Forty minutes before Harbor City went dark.
crisis:2.cnHint: 全城通讯____爆发，阿栗说我们只有四十分钟找到零点。
crisis:2.hook: Somewhere below us, a backup generator hummed to life uninvited.
crisis:2.line: 'This *crisis* did not start tonight — Zero has been cutting wires for weeks,' Ali said.

gather:2.en: The old port warehouse smelled of salt and dead signals. I watched through cracked glass as figures began to *gather* in the shadows below — ten, then twenty, each one pressing a folded note to their chest like a secret wound. Ali touched my arm. 'They all got the same message,' she whispered.
gather:2.cnHint: 我透过破损的玻璃，看见人们在仓库阴影中____，每人手持同一张折叠纸条。
gather:2.hook: The last figure to arrive wore Zero's coat.
gather:2.line: 'They *gather* here every time a forbidden word breaks through the grid.'

imagine:2.en: The encrypted file held only a sketch — a door drawn in red ink, no address, no name. I tried to *imagine* where in Harbor City a door like that could exist, but the city had ten thousand doors and half of them were lies. Ali slid a second sketch across the table.
imagine:2.cnHint: 加密文件里只有一幅画，我试图____它在现实中对应的地点。
imagine:2.hook: The second sketch showed my own face on the other side of the door.
imagine:2.line: 'Can you *imagine* a lock that only opens when you speak the right forbidden word?'

instance:2.en: Grey Crow laid three evidence cards on the wet concrete floor. 'Each one is an *instance* of the same pattern,' he said, tapping the cards without looking at me. Signal burst at midnight. A coded mark left behind. One witness gone by morning. I stared at card three. The witness was Ali.
instance:2.cnHint: 灰鸦将三张证据卡排开，说明每张都是同一规律的____。
instance:2.hook: He flipped card four, the one he had kept hidden in his sleeve.
instance:2.line: 'This is not the first *instance* — Zero has done this before, in three other districts.'

numerous:2.en: The archive room under Pier Nine held *numerous* hard drives stacked from floor to ceiling, each one tagged with a date and a district name. Someone had been recording Harbor City's banned broadcasts for decades. The dust on every drive was thick — except on the ones from last night.
numerous:2.cnHint: 九号码头地下档案室存放着____个硬盘，但只有昨晚的那些没有落灰。
numerous:2.hook: A single wire ran from the fresh drives to a transmitter still warm to the touch.
numerous:2.line: '*Numerous* signals were sent last night — more than Zero has ever risked at once.'

puzzle:2.en: The coded graffiti on the tunnel wall was a *puzzle* I had been staring at for twenty minutes — a grid of symbols that almost looked like a map but kept folding back on itself. Then Grey Crow covered half of it with his hand, and suddenly the other half made perfect sense.
puzzle:2.cnHint: 隧道墙上的密码涂鸦像一个____，直到灰鸦用手遮住一半，答案才浮现。
puzzle:2.hook: The map pointed to a location that should have been underwater for thirty years.
puzzle:2.line: 'Every *puzzle* Zero leaves has one piece that is meant to be found — and one that is meant to mislead.'

remind:2.en: Ali pinned a torn page to the board next to the other clues. 'This should *remind* you of the Dry Dock case,' she said quietly. It did. Same paper stock, same faint chemical smell, same three blank lines at the bottom where a signature should have been. My chest went cold.
remind:2.cnHint: 阿栗将撕下的纸页钉在板上，说它应该会____我想起另一个旧案。
remind:2.hook: The Dry Dock case was officially closed — and the lead investigator had vanished.
remind:2.line: 'Does this *remind* you of anything, or am I the only one who sees the connection?'

truly:2.en: I had read Zero's intercepts for months and thought I understood the pattern. Standing in the relay room now, looking at the live feed, I realized I had *truly* understood nothing. The signals were not coded messages. They were questions — the same question, asked over and over, waiting for one answer.
truly:2.cnHint: 在中继室看到实时信号后，我才____意识到自己此前完全误解了零点的意图。
truly:2.hook: The question on every signal was directed at a name I recognized as my own.
truly:2.line: 'You have *truly* never asked yourself why Grey Crow chose you specifically for this case?'

valuable:2.en: The small metal case Ali pulled from behind the ventilation panel was sealed with a voice lock. Grey Crow looked at it once and stepped back. 'Whatever is inside is *valuable* enough that Zero left two traps just to protect the approach,' he said. The lock blinked green — it had already been opened.
valuable:2.cnHint: 阿栗找到的金属盒设有声控锁，灰鸦说盒内之物____到零点专门设了两道陷阱保护它。
valuable:2.hook: The case was empty, and the lining was still warm.
valuable:2.line: 'The most *valuable* thing in this city is not data — it is the one word Zero has never broadcast.'

writer:2.en: The sealed file in the archive room held one name: a *writer* who had hidden forbidden words inside legal news reports for twenty years. Grey Crow slid the file across the cold table. 'This person built a whole second language,' he said. 'Every story was a signal.' I stared at the photo. The face looked ordinary. Dangerous things always do.
writer:2.cnHint: 档案室里的封存文件揭示了一位____的秘密身份，他把禁忌信号藏在普通报道中长达二十年。
writer:2.hook: The photo on the file matched the face I had seen that morning.
writer:2.line: 'This *writer* hid more secrets than any hacker I have ever caught.'

addition:2.en: Ali found the old broadcast log first. In *addition* to the public signal, a second layer of code ran beneath every transmission — invisible unless you knew how to listen. I pressed my ear to the receiver. The hidden layer was still active. Someone had never stopped sending. The rain hit the window like a warning.
addition:2.cnHint: 阿里发现广播记录中除了公开信号之外，还有一个隐藏的____层，至今仍在运行。
addition:2.hook: The hidden signal carried a timestamp from just three minutes ago.
addition:2.line: 'In *addition* to the public feed, there is a second channel nobody was meant to find.'

alternative:2.en: Grey Crow laid two data chips on the desk. 'There is no good *alternative*,' he said quietly. 'Either we upload the decoded file to the open net, or Zero buries it forever.' I looked at both chips. One meant exposure. One meant silence. The neon outside buzzed and flickered, as if the city itself were making the choice.
alternative:2.cnHint: 引路人告诉我，除了公开解密文件，没有其他____，但每个选项都有代价。
alternative:2.hook: My hand moved toward one chip, then stopped halfway.
alternative:2.line: 'The only *alternative* to going public is letting Zero win tonight.'

amazing:2.en: Inside the locked server room, the wall was covered in coded graffiti — years of hidden messages layered on top of each other. It was *amazing* that no inspector had ever read them correctly; each line looked like ordinary street art. Ali photographed every inch. I began to hear the signals beneath the paint, rising like music. Then the door behind us clicked.
amazing:2.cnHint: 密室墙上多年的涂鸦藏着无数密信，令人____的是从未有人识破，直到我们到来。
amazing:2.hook: The click meant the door was locked — from the outside.
amazing:2.line: 'It is *amazing* that this room survived every sweep for thirty years.'

ease:2.en: Zero moved through the checkpoint with total *ease*, badge held loose, steps unhurried, as if the whole port belonged to him. I watched from the upper deck, jaw tight. He was carrying the drive. Ali touched my arm. 'We can still cut him off at gate nine,' she whispered. I was already moving, but Zero had already seen me.
ease:2.cnHint: 对手以令人不安的____通过了关卡，带着关键数据驱动器，而我们的时间正在耗尽。
ease:2.hook: Zero smiled at me across the crowd, and did not slow down.
ease:2.line: 'He passes every scanner with such *ease* — he must have someone on the inside.'

frequent:2.en: The repair shop on Dock Street looked ordinary, but *frequent* visits from unknown couriers had drawn a quiet flag in the city grid. I pulled the access log: eleven drops in one week, always after dark. Ali cross-checked the times against Zero's known routes. Every single one matched. I folded the printout and put it in my coat.
frequent:2.cnHint: 码头街修理铺因陌生快递员____出现而被系统标记，记录与对手的行踪完全吻合。
frequent:2.hook: The shop light was still on, and a shadow moved behind the glass.
frequent:2.line: '*Frequent* late-night drops to the same address — that is not a coincidence.'

hope:2.en: The last message on the dead terminal was short: 'If you find this, there is still *hope*.' Grey Crow had written it six months before he went dark. I read it twice, rain loud on the roof. He had known someone would come looking. He had left a thread on purpose. I pulled it, and the whole wall of the archive slid open.
hope:2.cnHint: 终端上的最后一条留言说还有____，是引路人在失踪前六个月故意留下的线索。
hope:2.hook: Behind the open wall was a room that should not have existed.
hope:2.line: 'He left this message as a sign of *hope* for whoever came after him.'

imply:2.en: The graffiti tag on the substation door looked simple — three lines, one circle. But Grey Crow said the shape was coded to *imply* a meeting point, a time, and a warning, all at once. I stared until I saw it. Harbor City spoke in layers. You just had to know which layer was talking. My earpiece crackled. Ali's voice: 'Zero is already there.'
imply:2.cnHint: 变电站门上看似简单的涂鸦实则____着集合地点、时间与警告，而对手已经先到了。
imply:2.hook: I ran, and every neon sign I passed seemed to repeat the same word: late.
imply:2.line: 'These three lines *imply* far more than they show — read them again, carefully.'

insist:2.en: The old server room smelled of burnt wire and forgotten code. Ali held up a cracked data chip. 'We should leave,' she said. But I *insist* on staying — something in the chip was still broadcasting, a faint pulse only I could hear. Someone had been here minutes ago.
insist:2.cnHint: 我____要留下来，因为那块芯片还在发出微弱的信号。
insist:2.hook: The signal spelled out a name — mine.
insist:2.line: 'I *insist* you read every byte on that chip before we move.'

investigation:2.en: Grey Crow dropped a sealed file on the wet table. 'Your *investigation* starts here,' he said, tapping a map of the North Dock. Red marks covered three blocks. I opened the file. The first page was blank — except for a single line of code burned into the paper by laser.
investigation:2.cnHint: 这份文件是我____的起点，但第一页只有一行神秘的代码。
investigation:2.line: 'Your *investigation* will cost you more than you think.'

limited:2.en: Ali's signal scanner beeped twice and went dark. 'Power is *limited*,' she warned, shaking the device. We had maybe ten minutes before the backup grid cut out and left us blind in the server tunnels below Harbor City. I counted the steps to the exit. Too many.
limited:2.cnHint: 电量____，我们在黑暗的隧道里只剩下十分钟。
limited:2.hook: Then the exit door blinked — locked.
limited:2.line: 'Our time is *limited* — stop reading and start running.'

listen:2.en: '*Listen*,' Grey Crow said, and the word hit like a command. I stopped moving. Deep in the wall behind the neon graffiti, a hidden speaker was whispering a looped number sequence — the same seven digits, over and over. Only I could parse its real meaning. It was an address.
listen:2.cnHint: 灰鸦叫我____，墙里有个扬声器在低声重复一串数字。
listen:2.hook: The address was the city's oldest prison.
listen:2.line: '*Listen* carefully — the signal only repeats three times.'

master:2.en: The hacker guild called him *Master* Zero, though no one said it to his face. I found his mark on a newly painted wall: a crow with a broken wing. Below it, one sentence in plain text — rare in a city of codes. It read: 'The game ends at dawn.' My clock showed 4:58 a.m.
master:2.cnHint: 黑客们私下叫零点____，而我在墙上发现了他留下的标记和一句明文警告。
master:2.hook: Dawn in Harbor City was exactly two minutes away.
master:2.line: 'Even a *master* leaves tracks if you know where to look.'

newly:2.en: A *newly* installed camera watched the north stairwell — its lens still wore a factory sticker. Someone had placed it in the last hour. I pulled Ali back into the shadow. The camera turned, slow and precise, and stopped pointing directly at the spot where we had just been standing.
newly:2.cnHint: 楼梯间有一个____安装的摄像头，它缓缓转向我们刚才站立的位置。
newly:2.hook: Its red light blinked once — a signal, not a warning.
newly:2.line: 'That *newly* placed camera was not put there by the city.'

obviously:2.en: The decrypted note was short: meet at the dry dock, midnight, come alone. *Obviously* it was a trap — the ink was still wet, the dock had been sealed for a year, and Zero never used plain language. But the note also carried a second signal, buried deep, meant only for ears like mine. That changed everything.
obviously:2.cnHint: 这张纸条____是个陷阱，但纸条里还藏着一个只有我能听见的深层信号。
obviously:2.hook: The buried signal was Ali's voice.
obviously:2.line: '*Obviously* he wants you there — the question is why he wants you alone.'

mix:2.en: The evidence locker held a strange *mix* of objects: a cracked data chip, three sheets of coded paper, and a small glass bottle with no label. Ali spread them on the table under the cold blue light. Each item alone meant nothing. Together, they formed a pattern I almost recognised.
mix:2.cnHint: 证物室里有一批奇怪的____：一块破损的数据芯片、三张密码纸和一个无标签的小玻璃瓶。
mix:2.hook: The pattern pointed to an address that should not exist.
mix:2.line: 'This *mix* of objects is not random — someone left it for us.'

necessity:2.en: The server room was burning. I had thirty seconds. Grey Crow's voice cut through the smoke: copying the full drive was out of the question. The *necessity* of choosing only one file felt like a trap. I grabbed the folder marked ZERO and ran.
necessity:2.cnHint: 服务器机房起火了，侦探意识到只拿一个文件是绝对的____，于是抓起标有ZERO的文件夹逃跑。
necessity:2.hook: Outside, a black vehicle was already waiting with its engine running.
necessity:2.line: 'Speed is a luxury — *necessity* means you take only what matters.'

stuff:2.en: Grey Crow slid a sealed bag across the counter. Inside was soft grey *stuff*, almost like clay, pressed into the shape of a key. 'It holds a signal,' they said quietly. I pressed my finger against it and heard a voice — Zero's voice — begin to count down from ten.
stuff:2.cnHint: 灰鸦交给侦探一袋像黏土一样的____，里面藏着一段倒计时信号。
stuff:2.hook: At zero, the counting stopped — and every light in the building went out.
stuff:2.line: 'Don't drop it — this *stuff* carries the last known signal trace.'

translate:2.en: The graffiti covered the entire back wall of the old port warehouse. Ali said it was just street art. But when I let my mind go quiet, I could *translate* the layered colours into coordinates — latitude, longitude, and a time stamp set for midnight tonight.
translate:2.cnHint: 仓库墙上的涂鸦看似普通街头艺术，但侦探能将颜色____成今晚午夜的经纬度坐标。
translate:2.hook: Someone had painted those coordinates three days before the blackout.
translate:2.line: 'Only you can *translate* this — the colours shift meaning for each reader.'

wander:2.en: My orders were clear: stay in the east district. But the signal pulled me west, past the night markets and the broken bridge. I let myself *wander* for exactly four minutes — long enough to find the chalk mark on the pillar that Ali said was impossible to find.
wander:2.cnHint: 侦探违反命令，在城市中____了四分钟，却在桥墩上发现了那个据说不可能找到的粉笔记号。
wander:2.hook: The chalk was still wet — whoever drew it had left seconds ago.
wander:2.line: 'If you *wander* off the route again, Zero will know you are looking.'

warn:2.en: The message arrived as a burst of static on my earpiece, just three words hidden in the noise. Grey Crow had taken a risk to *warn* me: the meeting point was already watched. I changed direction without breaking stride, turning into a lane full of hanging red lights.
warn:2.cnHint: 灰鸦冒险发来信息，____侦探说接头地点已被监视，侦探悄然改变了方向。
warn:2.hook: Behind me, steady footsteps matched my pace exactly.
warn:2.line: 'I had to *warn* you — they changed the watch schedule an hour ago.'

cite:2.en: Ali pulled up the archived broadcast log and began to read aloud. Every line she chose to *cite* had one thing in common: the speaker had disappeared within a week of saying it. By the seventh entry, the pattern was impossible to ignore, and the room felt several degrees colder.
cite:2.cnHint: 阿栗从档案广播记录中逐条____，被引用的每位发言者都在一周内失踪，规律令人不寒而栗。
cite:2.hook: The eighth name on the list was Grey Crow's.
cite:2.line: 'I can *cite* seven cases — every one ends the same way.'

belong:2.en: The sealed file had no name on it, no case number, no stamp. Grey Crow slid it across the wet table. 'Read the first line,' he said. I did. My hands went cold. Every word in that file seemed to *belong* to a case I was never meant to find — a case that had my name buried at the bottom.
belong:2.cnHint: 调查员发现一份神秘文件，其中的内容似乎____于一桩她从未应该触碰的案子。
belong:2.hook: And the last line named someone who was standing right behind me.
belong:2.line: 'These records *belong* to a file that should not exist.'

beneficial:2.en: Ali pulled the data chip from the drain pipe and held it to the neon light. 'Dirty little thing,' she said. The chip held a list of chemicals — each one labeled *beneficial* for signal enhancement. But I knew those compounds. Mixed together, they did not help signals. They erased minds.
beneficial:2.cnHint: 阿里找到一块芯片，上面将某些化学物质标注为对信号____，但调查员认出了它们真正的用途。
beneficial:2.hook: Someone had been testing those compounds on Harbor City's night-shift workers for six months.
beneficial:2.line: 'They called each one *beneficial*, but look what they built with them.'

characteristic:2.en: Zero left a message burned into the wall of the empty server room — not words, just a pattern of dots. Grey Crow crouched and studied it. 'This spacing,' he said quietly, 'is a *characteristic* of only one encoder in the city.' He stood and looked at me. His face said everything his mouth would not.
characteristic:2.cnHint: 零点在墙上留下了一串暗号，灰鸦辨认出这是某个特定编码者的____。
characteristic:2.hook: That encoder had been reported dead for two years.
characteristic:2.line: 'That dot-gap pattern is a *characteristic* only Zero uses.'

director:2.en: The badge on the desk read: Office of Signal Control. I had broken in at midnight, rain loud on the roof. Inside a locked drawer I found a letter signed by someone called the *director* — ordering all investigators like me to be quietly removed from their posts before dawn on Friday. Today was Thursday.
director:2.cnHint: 调查员潜入办公室，发现一封____签署的信件，命令在黎明前清除所有像她这样的调查员。
director:2.line: 'The *director* signed the order at noon — while you were in this building.'

emerge:2.en: I watched the tunnel entrance for twenty minutes. Nothing moved. Then, slowly, a figure began to *emerge* from the dark — first a hand, then a coat, then a face I had seen only in classified files. Ali grabbed my arm. 'That is not possible,' she whispered. 'That person died in the harbour last year.'
emerge:2.cnHint: 一个应该已经死去的人开始从黑暗中____，阿里紧紧抓住了调查员的手臂。
emerge:2.hook: The figure raised one hand and pointed directly at me.
emerge:2.line: 'Watch the door — something is about to *emerge* and it is not on our side.'

exact:2.en: Grey Crow handed me a printed map of the underground cable lines. 'Zero will hit one of these nodes,' he said. 'But which one?' Ali ran the numbers twice. 'I have the *exact* point,' she said, marking a circle near the old port. 'Sub-level three. Junction nine.' We had forty minutes.
exact:2.cnHint: 阿里经过计算，找到了零点将要发动袭击的____位置，距离行动只剩四十分钟。
exact:2.hook: When we reached sub-level three, the junction was already open — and warm.
exact:2.line: 'I have the *exact* location. We move now or we lose him.'

guest:2.en: The signal café near Dock Seven looked normal — soft light, low voices, rain on the glass. But every seat was taken by someone who never ordered anything. Grey Crow leaned close. 'Each one is a *guest* of Zero,' he said. 'They are waiting for a broadcast that will rewrite their access codes.' I counted twelve of them.
guest:2.cnHint: 信号咖啡馆里的每一位____都是零点的人，他们正在等待一次能重写权限代码的广播。
guest:2.hook: Then the lights went out and the broadcast began.
guest:2.line: 'Every *guest* in this room is carrying a live receiver — check under the tables.'

massive:2.en: Ali cracked the last encryption layer and the screen filled with data. A *massive* grid of names, dates, and signal codes covered every inch of the display — thousands of citizens, each one tagged with a hidden broadcast ID. Zero had not been building a weapon. Zero had been building an audience. I felt the floor shift under me.
massive:2.cnHint: 阿里破解加密后，屏幕上出现了____的数据网格，零点原来一直在悄悄建立一个庞大的受众群体。
massive:2.hook: And every name on that list had received a signal in the last hour.
massive:2.line: 'This is a *massive* network — Zero has been growing it for three years.'

pose:2.en: The dead drop was a cracked mirror in sub-level nine. Someone had left a photograph tucked behind it — a figure caught mid-*pose*, arms wide, back to the camera, facing the city grid. On the back, three words in red: 'Find the angle.' I knew that stance. I had seen it before, on a rooftop, in the rain.
pose:2.cnHint: 调查员在废弃镜子后找到一张照片，照片里的人____引发了他的记忆。
pose:2.hook: The figure in the photograph was wearing my coat.
pose:2.line: 'That *pose* is a signal — someone is marking a location for us.'

stimulate:2.en: Grey Crow slid a data chip across the wet table. 'The city council uses banned frequencies to *stimulate* fear,' he said quietly. 'Low signal, deep range. People feel uneasy and never know why.' I plugged the chip into my reader. The waveform on the screen looked like a heartbeat — but wrong, too slow, too deliberate.
stimulate:2.cnHint: 灰鸦向调查员解释市政委员会如何用禁播信号____民众，使其感到恐惧。
stimulate:2.hook: The waveform on my reader matched the signal in my own skull.
stimulate:2.line: 'They use it to *stimulate* panic — invisible, untraceable, and everywhere.'

switch:2.en: Ali found the relay box bolted inside a noodle stall on Deck Four. One *switch*, she said, controls every public screen in the harbor district. Flip it and Zero's message plays city-wide. Leave it and the blackout holds. I stared at the small lever. Outside, rain hammered the steel roof like a countdown.
switch:2.cnHint: 阿栗发现了一个____，能控制整个港区的公共屏幕，调查员必须做出抉择。
switch:2.hook: Someone had already flipped it halfway.
switch:2.line: 'One *switch* and the whole city sees the truth — or loses it forever.'

treatment:2.en: The file was stamped LEVEL ZERO — CLOSED. Inside: medical records, six names, all former signal analysts. Each had received the same *treatment* at the city's central data clinic — a procedure listed only as 'acoustic correction.' All six had gone silent after. No more reports. No more complaints. I was a signal analyst too.
treatment:2.cnHint: 调查员发现一份档案，记录着六名分析员接受同一种____后全部销声匿迹。
treatment:2.hook: My own name was penciled in at the bottom of the list.
treatment:2.line: 'The *treatment* looks medical — but it is designed to erase what people hear.'

union:2.en: The graffiti covered the entire east wall of the old port terminal: a circle broken in two, rejoined by a single line. Grey Crow traced it with one finger. 'That is the mark of the *union*,' he said. 'Hackers, codebreakers, rogue analysts — they have been building this for years.' I felt the signal hum in my jaw, louder than before.
union:2.cnHint: 灰鸦向调查员解释港口墙上的涂鸦是某个秘密____的标志。
union:2.hook: The hum in my jaw shaped itself into a single word: run.
union:2.line: 'The *union* has been waiting for someone who can hear the hidden signals.'

acknowledge:2.en: Zero left a voice packet buried in a public weather broadcast. I ran it through my filter and heard the real message underneath: calm, clear, almost polite. 'I know you found the file. I know you read the names. Now *acknowledge* that you understand — or the clinic gets your address tonight.' I sat very still. The rain outside had stopped.
acknowledge:2.cnHint: 零点在广播中留下密语，要求调查员____自己已经明白了威胁的含义。
acknowledge:2.hook: My hand moved toward the transmit key on its own.
acknowledge:2.line: '*Acknowledge* the message and they will know you are alone and afraid.'

alike:2.en: Ali spread the two intercepts side by side on the floor. The signal patterns looked *alike* at first — same rhythm, same gap between pulses. But she circled one difference: a single extra beat, every twelfth cycle, too regular to be noise. 'That beat is a name,' she said. I leaned closer. The name belonged to someone I trusted completely.
alike:2.cnHint: 阿栗发现两份看似____的信号截图里藏着一个关键差异，指向了一个意想不到的名字。
alike:2.hook: The name in the signal was Grey Crow.
alike:2.line: 'They look *alike* on purpose — you are supposed to miss the difference.'

analyze:2.en: The message came as a torn label stuck to my door: seven symbols, no spaces, no obvious language. Grey Crow said nothing — just handed me a pen. I had to *analyze* the pattern alone, the way he had taught me. Forty minutes later, cold and tired, I saw it: the symbols were not letters. They were a map of sub-level nine.
analyze:2.cnHint: 调查员独自____门上留下的神秘符号，最终发现那是一张地图。
analyze:2.hook: The map led straight to the door I was already standing behind.
analyze:2.line: '*Analyze* it slowly — the answer is hidden in what seems like noise.'

content:2.en: The sealed drive finally opened. Inside: thousands of stolen voice files, sorted by district, by date, by speaker. I scanned the list and felt something cold settle in my chest. Grey Crow had warned me the archive would be ugly. He was right. But one file near the bottom made me anything but *content* — it carried my own voice, recorded three weeks before I joined the agency.
content:2.cnHint: 调查员在档案底部发现了一个令人不安的文件，让他无法感到____。
content:2.hook: Someone had been watching me long before I was watching them.
content:2.line: 'You look *content* with what you found — you shouldn't be.'

divide:2.en: The old port map on the wall showed Harbor City split into two zones: the Signal Side and the Dead Side. A thick red line ran between them like a scar. Ali traced it with one finger. 'That line used to be a river,' she said. Every crime we had logged this month fell on one side of the *divide* — the side where the city's voice filters went dark at midnight.
divide:2.cnHint: 阿栗在地图上指出，本月所有案件都发生在城市____的同一侧。
divide:2.hook: Whatever was silencing those filters lived right on that line.
divide:2.line: 'Every signal we lost sits on the wrong side of the *divide*.'

generate:2.en: Zero's transmitter was small enough to hide in a coat button. Ali found it taped under the bench in locker seven. The device could *generate* a false identity signal strong enough to fool the city's ID scanners for up to six hours. Six hours was more than enough time to vanish, or to become someone else entirely. The battery was still warm.
generate:2.cnHint: 阿栗发现了零点用来____虚假身份信号的装置，电池还是热的。
generate:2.hook: Whoever used it last had left only minutes ago.
generate:2.line: 'This thing can *generate* a fake ID signal that beats every scanner in the port.'

operate:2.en: The terminal in the basement looked dead — dark screen, no hum. Then Ali pressed two keys at once and it woke with a pale blue glow. 'Grey Crow taught me how to *operate* this model,' she said quietly, her eyes never leaving the screen. It was running a live feed from inside the Harbor City Signal Authority. Someone had left a door open on purpose.
operate:2.cnHint: 阿栗知道如何____这台地下终端，屏幕上显示的是信号局的实时画面。
operate:2.hook: The open door was either a gift or a trap — no way to know which.
operate:2.line: 'I know how to *operate* it — Grey Crow showed me the sequence himself.'

properly:2.en: The coded note had been folded four times and sealed with a plain sticker. I opened it at the table under the yellow lamp. The characters were standard port script, but the spacing was off. Nothing was *properly* aligned — every third word sat half a beat too far right. That was the key. Read only the shifted words and you got a time, a gate number, and one name: Zero.
properly:2.cnHint: 调查员发现纸条上的文字没有____对齐，错位的词语隐藏着一条秘密信息。
properly:2.hook: The meeting was set for one hour from now, and I was alone.
properly:2.line: 'Nothing here is *properly* spaced — someone built a message into the gaps.'

render:2.en: Grey Crow slid a thin card across the table without a word. It looked blank. I held it under the UV lamp above the sink and the surface lit up — a dense grid of micro-text, every line a frequency, every frequency a name. Exposure to UV light would *render* the ink visible for exactly ninety seconds before it faded back to nothing. I had a pen and no time to waste.
render:2.cnHint: 灰鸦给的卡片在紫外线下会____隐藏的文字可见，但只有九十秒。
render:2.hook: My hand was already moving but the lines were fading faster than I could copy.
render:2.line: 'UV light will *render* the text visible — you have ninety seconds, not more.'

resolve:2.en: I stood at the end of the corridor for a long moment, rain loud on the roof, the drive in my coat pocket, Zero's last signal still ringing in my ear. Every path forward had a cost. But doubt was a luxury I had already spent. I fixed my *resolve*, stepped through the door, and let it lock behind me. No exit now — only the next move, and whatever waited on the other side.
resolve:2.cnHint: 调查员在走廊尽头下定____，迈步走入房间，身后的门随之锁上。
resolve:2.hook: The click of the lock was the loudest sound in Harbor City that night.
resolve:2.line: 'Fix your *resolve* now — once we cross that line there is no coming back.'

seemingly:2.en: The broadcast came through on a clean channel at exactly midnight — calm music, soft and low, the kind that plays in empty waiting rooms. *Seemingly* harmless, the kind of noise the city filters ignored by design. But underneath the melody, threaded into the lowest frequency, Ali caught a repeating pattern: eleven pulses, pause, three pulses, pause, seven. A countdown, or a code. Neither answer was good.
seemingly:2.cnHint: 那段____无害的广播音乐，在最低频率中隐藏着阿栗察觉到的重复信号。
seemingly:2.hook: Ali's face went pale the moment she worked out what the numbers meant.
seemingly:2.line: 'It sounds *seemingly* normal — that is exactly why I almost missed it.'

therefore:2.en: The abandoned signal tower on Pier 9 had gone silent for three years. Tonight, its light blinked twice — the old distress code. Grey Crow pressed a folded note into my hand: the tower was compromised, and *therefore* every safe route on the eastern docks was now suspect.
therefore:2.cnHint: 信号塔重新亮起，灰鸦认为____所有东码头的安全路线都不可信了。
therefore:2.hook: Someone wanted us moving — straight into the open.
therefore:2.line: 'The tower is burned, and *therefore* we trust no map made before midnight.'

truth:2.en: Ali pulled a cracked data chip from beneath a loose floor tile in the old customs hall. The chip held one file: a recording of Zero's voice, calm and certain, admitting everything. 'This is the *truth* they buried,' Ali whispered, hand shaking as the audio played on.
truth:2.cnHint: 阿栗在海关大厅地砖下发现了一块芯片，里面藏着令人震惊的____。
truth:2.hook: But the file's timestamp was three hours from now.
truth:2.line: 'I found the *truth* — and it hasn't happened yet.'

protein:2.en: The night market stall sold hot bowls of grey broth. Grey Crow pointed at the label on the canister behind the counter: a banned synthetic *protein* formula, the same compound Zero's network used to smuggle data capsules through the city's food checkpoints. We had our entry point.
protein:2.cnHint: 夜市摊位的肉汤罐头上贴着违禁____配方标签，这正是零点走私数据的通道。
protein:2.hook: The cook reached under the counter without being asked.
protein:2.line: 'Every capsule rides inside a *protein* shell — customs never checks the food line.'

traffic:2.en: From the overpass, Harbor City's *traffic* below looked like slow blood in a clogged vein — delivery drones, cargo carts, and coded courier bikes all funnelled through Checkpoint Seven. Grey Crow said Zero's package was already in that stream. We had four minutes to find it.
traffic:2.cnHint: 灰鸦说零点的包裹就混在检查站七号的____人流中，我们只有四分钟。
traffic:2.hook: A green courier bike peeled away from the queue and accelerated hard.
traffic:2.line: 'Watch the *traffic* — Zero's package is already moving through Checkpoint Seven.'

cat:2.en: The only living thing in the abandoned data vault was a thin grey *cat*, sitting on a humming server rack as if it owned the room. Ali noticed its collar first — a tiny copper tag engraved with coordinates. Someone had used the animal as a living dead drop.
cat:2.cnHint: 废弃数据仓库里，一只____的项圈上刻着某个关键坐标。
cat:2.hook: The cat turned its head toward the far wall and did not blink.
cat:2.line: 'Don't scare it — that *cat* is carrying the only copy of the address.'

sugar:2.en: The coded graffiti on the sub-level wall read clean to any passing officer, but Grey Crow traced the letters slowly. '*Sugar*,' he murmured — street slang for a bribe log, a list of every official Zero had paid off. The wall itself was a confession, hidden in plain sight.
sugar:2.cnHint: 地下通道墙上的涂鸦里，____一词是行贿记录的暗语，藏着零点收买官员的名单。
sugar:2.hook: One name on that list made Grey Crow go very still.
sugar:2.line: 'In this district, *sugar* on a wall means someone powerful has already been paid.'

balance:2.en: The rooftop relay dish tilted in the wind, and the encrypted feed it carried kept cutting out. I had to *balance* on the narrow service rail, arms wide, to reach the cable junction without knocking the dish offline. One wrong shift and Zero's signal — our only lead — was gone.
balance:2.cnHint: 我必须在狭窄的维修栏杆上____身体，才能接触到电缆接口而不破坏信号。
balance:2.hook: The wind picked up the moment my fingers touched the wire.
balance:2.line: '*Balance* — if that dish moves even one degree, we lose the feed forever.'

baby:2.en: The note tucked inside the locker read: 'Don't play *baby* — this is the last warning.' It was signed with Zero's mark. Ali stared at it, jaw tight. The locker belonged to a port inspector who had been feeding us information for weeks. His last check-in was forty hours ago.
baby:2.cnHint: 储物柜里的纸条用零点的标记署名，警告某人不要____，而我们的线人已失联四十小时。
baby:2.hook: Ali's hand moved to the locker's lower shelf and found it empty.
baby:2.line: 'Don't go *baby* on me now — Zero left that note inside an hour ago.'

teenager:2.en: The message was carved into a school desk — not random damage, but code. A *teenager* had sat here recently; the ink on the carved letters was still fresh. Grey Crow had told me young runners were Zero's best messengers. Nobody watches a kid. I photographed every word before the cleaners arrived.
teenager:2.cnHint: 一个年轻的____刚刚在这张课桌上刻下了密码信息，墨迹未干。
teenager:2.hook: The last carved word was my own name.
teenager:2.line: 'A *teenager* carved that message — Zero is recruiting younger every cycle.'

patient:2.en: Ali slid a folded note under the door of the clinic's waiting room. The *patient* list on the wall was fake — each name a dead-drop code. I cross-checked three entries and found a pickup time buried in the diagnosis column. Zero had been using this place for months.
patient:2.cnHint: 诊所墙上的____名单是伪装成医疗记录的密码，我从中找到了接头时间。
patient:2.hook: The fourth name on the list was Ali's.
patient:2.line: 'Be *patient* — the real message is hidden in the last diagnosis entry.'

classroom:2.en: The abandoned *classroom* on Level Nine smelled of old paper and burnt wire. Someone had rewritten every equation on the board using Zero's cipher alphabet. Ali recognised two of the symbols. I copied the rest fast — the building's sensor net had just switched back on.
classroom:2.cnHint: 废弃____的黑板上，每一道方程式都被改写成了密码字符。
classroom:2.hook: The sensor log showed Grey Crow had been here an hour before us.
classroom:2.line: 'This *classroom* is Zero's message board — every equation is an order.'

vehicle:2.en: Grey Crow left the key inside a hollow tile near the east dock. The *vehicle* it opened was unmarked, engine already warm — someone had used it minutes ago. Under the seat I found a sealed chip wrapped in a hand-drawn map of the harbor's lower tunnels.
vehicle:2.cnHint: 灰鸦藏在瓷砖里的钥匙打开了一辆____，座椅下藏着一张手绘地图。
vehicle:2.hook: The map had a route marked in the same ink as the coded graffiti downtown.
vehicle:2.line: 'That *vehicle* was Zero's — check every panel for hidden compartments.'

remote:2.en: The signal came from a *remote* server node buried three layers below Harbor City's public grid. Grey Crow had warned me about ghost nodes — illegal, untraceable, perfect for Zero. I locked the frequency and began recording. The broadcast was only thirty seconds long.
remote:2.cnHint: 信号来自城市公共网络深处一个____的非法服务器节点。
remote:2.hook: The final second of the broadcast was my own voice, played back to me.
remote:2.line: 'That *remote* node has been live for six months — Zero planned this long ago.'

zoo:2.en: The meeting point was the old *zoo* on Harbor Hill, closed since the floods of 2071. Ali found a metal case chained to the main gate — inside, a drive and a single printed line: GREY CROW KNOWS THE PRICE. Zero had been watching our every step.
zoo:2.cnHint: 在废弃的____大门上，阿栗发现了一个金属箱，里面装着驱动器和一条警告。
zoo:2.hook: The chain lock used a code only I was supposed to know.
zoo:2.line: 'The *zoo* drop was never meant for us — someone intercepted Grey Crow's route.'

card:2.en: Tucked inside a cracked junction box near the night market, I found a small *card* — blank on one side, micro-printed on the other. Under my scanner it resolved into a floor plan of Zero's relay station. Grey Crow had left it three days ago. The timing felt wrong.
card:2.cnHint: 在夜市附近的配电箱里，我找到了一张____，扫描后显示出零点中继站的平面图。
card:2.hook: The floor plan showed a room that did not appear on any official record.
card:2.line: 'That *card* holds the only map of Zero's inner relay — guard it with your life.'
