assign:2.hook: The order had been signed three days before the case even existed.
assign:2.line: 'They *assign* solo cases only when they want someone to disappear quietly.'

broad:2.en: Zero's broadcast ran on a *broad* frequency — wide open, meant to be caught by every scanner in Harbor City. That was the trick. While every investigator chased that obvious signal, the real message was threading through a single hair-thin channel none of us had thought to watch.
broad:2.cnHint: 零点故意用____的频段广播作为诱饵，真正的信息却藏在一条无人注意的细窄信道里。
broad:2.hook: I had already wasted four hours chasing the decoy.
broad:2.line: 'A *broad* signal is always bait — look for the one channel that is too quiet.'

careful:2.en: Ali was *careful* — meticulous in a way that border on fear. Every slip of paper was folded twice before burning. Every word was chosen like a tool for a specific lock. So when I found Ali's notebook left open on the table, its pages facing the window, I knew it was not an accident.
careful:2.cnHint: 阿栗向来____到近乎恐惧，所以那本敞开摆在窗边的笔记本绝不是无意间遗忘的。
careful:2.hook: The page it was open to showed only my face, sketched in grey ink.
careful:2.line: 'Be *careful* with that page — it is the only copy of what we found in the server.'

combination:2.en: The vault under the old signal tower needed a *combination* of two things to open: a numeric code and a spoken word in the correct frequency. Grey Crow had the code. I had the word lodged in my skull like a splinter. Together we stood in the dark, rain loud on the iron roof above us.
combination:2.cnHint: 旧信号塔下的保险库需要数字密码与特定音频的____才能开启，灰鸦和我各持一半。
combination:2.hook: The vault clicked — then something inside it moved on its own.
combination:2.line: 'The lock responds to a *combination* of voice and code — neither of us can open it alone.'

constant:2.en: The interference was *constant* — an unbroken hum threaded through every channel I owned, never rising, never falling, steady as a held breath. Ali said it meant someone had locked onto my signal and was simply waiting. Not jamming. Not attacking. Just watching, with the patience of someone who already knew how the story ended.
constant:2.cnHint: 干扰信号____地持续着，阿栗说这意味着有人已经锁定了我的频道，只是在静静等待。
constant:2.hook: Then the hum stopped — and the silence was far worse.
constant:2.line: 'The watch on you has been *constant* for six hours — they are not in a hurry because they think you cannot escape.'

consultant:2.en: The sub-basement archive smelled of rust and old paper. A name badge lay on the floor: DR. VOSS, LANGUAGE *CONSULTANT*. Ali picked it up, fingers cold. Someone had been paid to study our signals — not to stop them, but to sell their secrets. The badge was still warm.
consultant:2.cnHint: 地下档案室里，我们发现了一个神秘____的证件，他似乎出卖了我们的信号。
consultant:2.hook: The photo on the badge matched a face we already knew.
consultant:2.line: 'A *consultant* who sells secrets is just a spy with better pay,' Ali said.

direct:2.en: Grey Crow spread the decoded map across the wet table. Every signal route in Harbor City was charted — but one line ran *direct* from the port to the Council tower, no relay, no trace. No one should have had access to that channel. Someone at the top was listening from the start.
direct:2.cnHint: 灰鸦发现了一条____通往议会塔的信号线路，这意味着有人从一开始就在监听。
direct:2.hook: The line had been open for exactly three years — since my first day on the job.
direct:2.line: 'This *direct* link means the leak is not outside — it is inside,' Grey Crow said.

discourage:2.en: Zero left a message burned into the wall of the signal relay on Level Nine: STOP NOW. The words were meant to *discourage* anyone still searching. Ali read them twice, then looked at me with steady eyes and shook her head. We had come too far to turn back over scorched paint.
discourage:2.cnHint: 零点在信号站墙上留下警告，试图____我们，但阿栗毫不动摇。
discourage:2.hook: Below the warning, scratched in tiny letters, was a single word: 'please.'
discourage:2.line: 'Nothing will *discourage* us now — not words, not fire,' Ali said quietly.

essentially:2.en: The cipher Zero used was *essentially* a language inside a language — common Harbor words rearranged by a key only two people had ever held. I had cracked the outer shell in an hour. The inner key, though, was still dark. One door open, one door sealed, and the clock on the wall still running.
essentially:2.cnHint: 零点使用的密码____是一种语言中的语言，我破解了外层，但内层钥匙仍是谜。
essentially:2.hook: Grey Crow said only one person alive still knew that inner key.
essentially:2.line: 'It is *essentially* a trap built from words — careful how you read it,' Grey Crow warned.

extent:2.en: The fog report from the harbor drone showed the *extent* of the blackout: fourteen city blocks, every signal dead, every camera blind. It was not a power fault. It was a planned silence, cut with precision. Someone had drawn a clean dark square over exactly the blocks we needed to cross tonight.
extent:2.cnHint: 无人机报告揭示了信号中断的____，整整十四个街区，一片黑暗，像是精心设计的。
extent:2.hook: The blackout was scheduled to end in twenty minutes — with or without us inside.
extent:2.line: 'The *extent* of this blackout tells me they knew our route,' Grey Crow said.

finance:2.en: Buried in the archive was a single ledger page. Every secret broadcast in Harbor City for the past two years had been funded by one source. The entry read: COUNCIL SPECIAL FUND. The Council did not merely ignore the signal network — they chose to *finance* it. They built the cage they now pretended to fear.
finance:2.cnHint: 档案中的账本揭示，议会竟然____了这整个秘密广播网络。
finance:2.hook: The signature at the bottom belonged to the officer now leading the investigation against us.
finance:2.line: 'They *finance* the very crime they hunt — that is the oldest trick in power,' Grey Crow said.

highlight:2.en: Zero's final file was mostly noise — static, broken dates, dead addresses. But one section was different. Grey Crow ran a filter and watched the screen: a single clean paragraph rose from the garbage, as if Zero had chosen to *highlight* it for whoever came looking. It named a time, a place, and one of us.
highlight:2.cnHint: 零点留下的文件中，灰鸦用过滤器找到一段被____的段落，其中点名了我们其中一人。
highlight:2.hook: The name in that paragraph was mine.
highlight:2.line: 'Zero chose to *highlight* this for a reason — read every word twice,' Grey Crow said.

himself:2.en: The coded letter had no signature. But the style — sharp, cold, precise — told me everything. Zero had written it *himself*, without using any of his usual tricks. No false names. No ghost writers. Just him, raw and exposed, daring me to find him.
himself:2.cnHint: 那封密信没有署名，但我认出了笔迹背后的人：零点____写下了它。
himself:2.hook: The last line of the letter was my home address.
himself:2.line: 'He sent it *himself* — no middleman, no cover. That means he wants to be found.'

landscape:2.en: Ali pulled up the city grid on her screen. The *landscape* of Harbor City spread before us — a maze of neon towers, black canals, and dead signal zones. Somewhere inside that glowing map, Zero had hidden the final key. We had one hour to find it.
landscape:2.cnHint: 阿栗在屏幕上展开了海港城的地图____，我们必须在这片迷宫中找到那把钥匙。
landscape:2.hook: Then a whole city block vanished from the map.
landscape:2.line: 'Study this *landscape* carefully — one wrong turn and we lose him forever.'

mentally:2.en: Grey Crow handed me the encrypted file and said nothing. I closed my eyes and *mentally* traced each symbol, each gap, each silent beat in the code. The pattern was there. It always was. But this time, it felt like a trap set just for me.
mentally:2.cnHint: 我____在脑海中逐一梳理那串密码，试图找出隐藏的规律。
mentally:2.hook: The final symbol was not a letter — it was my badge number.
mentally:2.line: 'I *mentally* mapped the whole sequence. Something about it is designed to mislead you.'

neither:2.en: Grey Crow looked at the two drives on the table. '*Neither* of these is the real one,' he said quietly. I stared at them. Both looked identical. Both were clean. If the true drive was somewhere else, Zero had already moved it — and we had just wasted our only lead.
neither:2.cnHint: 桌上两块硬盘，灰鸦说____是真正的目标，这意味着零点早已转移了真品。
neither:2.hook: Then the lights in the room cut to black.
neither:2.line: '*Neither* path is safe — but one of them leads to the truth.'

onto:2.en: Ali patched the signal *onto* the main screen. Static. Then a face — Zero's face, calm and cold, looking straight at us through the feed. He had hacked into our own display. He was not hiding anymore. He was watching us watch him.
onto:2.cnHint: 阿栗将信号投____主屏幕，零点的脸就这样出现在我们眼前。
onto:2.hook: Zero smiled, then the feed cut to a countdown.
onto:2.line: 'I pushed the signal *onto* the public grid — everyone in Harbor City can see it now.'

plus:2.en: Ali laid out the facts: one stolen cipher, *plus* a missing investigator, plus three dead signal towers on the east side. The numbers added up to one thing. Zero was not running. He was building something. And whatever it was, it would go live at midnight.
plus:2.cnHint: 一个被盗密码____三座失联信号塔，这些线索叠加起来指向一个可怕的计划。
plus:2.line: 'Two hidden nodes *plus* the main relay — that is enough to crash the whole city grid.'

root:2.en: Grey Crow knelt by the old terminal and brushed the dust away. 'The *root* command is still active,' he murmured. If that was true, whoever held this terminal held the city's entire signal network. Zero had not destroyed the system. He had buried himself inside it.
root:2.cnHint: 灰鸦发现旧终端的____命令仍然有效——零点已将自己藏入整个信号网络的核心。
root:2.hook: The screen flickered and typed one word: 'Hello.'
root:2.line: 'Find the *root* and you find him — he never left, he just went deeper.'

satisfy:2.en: Zero's message was brief: 'One question. Answer it correctly and I walk away. Fail, and Harbor City goes dark.' I read the question three times. It was simple — too simple. Whatever answer I gave, it would not *satisfy* him. This was never about the answer. It was about watching me choose.
satisfy:2.cnHint: 零点只提了一个问题，但我知道无论我如何作答，都无法____他——这是一个陷阱。
satisfy:2.hook: Ali grabbed my arm: 'Don't type anything yet.'
satisfy:2.line: 'Nothing you do will *satisfy* him — he built this game so no one can win.'

farmer:1.en: Rain hammered the street market. A hunched old man sold root vegetables from a mud-caked cart — too calm, too still for the chaos around him. Grey Crow pressed close. 'That *farmer* is not selling food,' he muttered. 'He is selling coordinates.' The cart's wooden slats hid a blinking transmitter.
farmer:1.cnHint: 灰鸦在街头市集发现那个卖菜的____并非普通人，他的推车里藏着信号发射器。
farmer:1.hook: The transmitter's light turned red and began to count down.
farmer:1.line: 'That *farmer* has been here every night this week — watch him.'

youth:1.en: Neon signs bled colour into the wet asphalt. Ali grabbed my sleeve and pointed at a figure spray-painting coded glyphs onto the tunnel wall — a kid, barely sixteen. 'Pure *youth*,' Ali whispered, 'and already deep in Zero's network.' The glyphs pulsed faintly, as if the wall itself was breathing.
youth:1.cnHint: 阿里指着隧道墙壁前正在涂鸦的少年，说那个____已经加入了零点的网络。
youth:1.hook: The kid turned, looked straight at us, and ran.
youth:1.line: 'His *youth* makes him useful — and very easy to replace.'

principle:0.en: Grey Crow spread the stolen files across the table. 'Every code has a *principle* behind it,' he said quietly. 'Find the rule, and the lock opens.' I studied the patterns. Somewhere in this room, the answer was already written. I just had to see it.
principle:0.cnHint: 灰鸦在室内向我解释，破解密码需要找到其背后的____。
principle:0.hook: The pattern shifted — and one file did not fit.
principle:0.line: 'Find the *principle*, and the whole system falls open.'

rat:0.en: The safe house felt wrong the moment I stepped inside. Ali knelt by the corner, her flashlight on a small dead *rat* near the vent. 'Someone left this here on purpose,' she whispered. A warning sign — or a message. Either way, we were already expected.
rat:0.cnHint: 阿栗在室内角落发现了一只死____，怀疑这是有人故意留下的警告。
rat:0.hook: Behind the vent, a red light blinked once, then went dark.
rat:0.line: 'A dead *rat* by the vent means someone was here before us.'

context:0.en: Zero's broadcast was thirty seconds of noise — until I slowed it down. Without *context*, the words meant nothing. But set against the building plans on the wall, each phrase mapped to a room, a time, a target. My hands went cold. This was not a threat. It was a countdown.
context:0.cnHint: 我在室内将零点的广播与墙上的图纸对照，终于在特定的____下读懂了其中含义。
context:0.hook: The last room on the map — that was where I was standing now.
context:0.line: 'Without *context*, the message is just noise — with it, it's a death list.'

flexible:0.en: The ventilation shaft was narrow and bent at sharp angles. Ali moved through it like water. 'You have to be *flexible*,' she called back, her voice tight but steady. I forced my shoulders flat and followed. Above us, Zero's crew swept the floors with lights. We had sixty seconds.
flexible:0.cnHint: 阿栗在通风管道内提醒我身体要____，因为零点的人正在楼上搜查。
flexible:0.hook: Sixty seconds — then a lock clicked somewhere below us.
flexible:0.line: 'Stay *flexible* or the shaft will trap you in there.'

oil:0.en: The server room smelled of burnt *oil* and old metal. Grey Crow pressed two fingers to the main unit. 'It overheated,' he said. 'Someone ran it hard and fast, then left.' The data was still warm. Whoever had been here had pulled something — and left minutes ago.
oil:0.cnHint: 灰鸦在服务器室闻到了烧焦的____气味，判断有人刚刚撤离。
oil:0.hook: On the floor, a single boot print pointed straight toward the exit.
oil:0.line: 'Smell that burnt *oil* — the machine was pushed to its limit.'

arise:0.en: I had run every possible plan. But problems always *arise* when the map meets the real world. The door Grey Crow marked as open was welded shut. Ali checked her device — no signal. We were cut off, one floor above Zero's position, with no route we had rehearsed.
arise:0.cnHint: 在室内，我们发现原定计划中从未预料到的麻烦____了，退路已被封死。
arise:0.hook: Ali's device flickered once — then showed Zero's signal, right beneath us.
arise:0.line: 'New problems *arise* every time — you adapt or you lose.'

advocate:2.en: Deep inside the server vault, I found a sealed file stamped CLASSIFIED. It named Grey Crow as the last *advocate* for open-signal rights — someone who fought hard so ordinary people could speak freely on the grid. Zero wanted that name buried. Now I held the proof.
advocate:2.cnHint: 我在密封档案里发现了灰鸦是自由信号权利____的证据。
advocate:2.hook: The file was already uploading somewhere I could not stop.
advocate:2.line: 'Grey Crow is the only *advocate* left — protect that file.'

formal:2.en: Ali slid a *formal* notice across the wet table — city seal, red ink, official codes. The document ordered all rogue signal operators to shut down within twenty-four hours. No appeal, no hearing. Zero had finally used the law as a weapon.
formal:2.cnHint: 阿栗带来了一份要求所有游离信号员关闭设备的____通知。
formal:2.hook: At the bottom, my own investigator number was circled in red.
formal:2.line: 'This *formal* order means they know exactly who we are.'

moral:2.en: Grey Crow's last broadcast was short: act on your own *moral* judgment, not on orders from above. I replayed those nine words three times in the rain. Zero had called it dangerous talk. Maybe that was the point.
moral:2.cnHint: 灰鸦的最后一段广播讲述了关于____判断的忠告。
moral:2.hook: The broadcast timestamp showed it was sent six minutes after his arrest.
moral:2.line: 'Your *moral* judgment is the only map you have left.'

quit:2.en: The terminal blinked once, then a single line appeared: OPERATOR GREY CROW HAS CHOSEN TO *QUIT*. Not captured. Not silenced. He walked away on his own. Ali stared at the screen. I felt the floor tilt under me.
quit:2.cnHint: 终端显示灰鸦主动____了，这让我们措手不及。
quit:2.hook: His access card was still warm on the keyboard.
quit:2.line: 'He did not *quit* — he left a door open for us.'

death:2.en: Hidden inside a cracked signal relay on the east pier, I found a small chip etched with one word: *death*. Below it, a list of seven names. Mine was number six. Ali touched my arm without speaking.
death:2.cnHint: 我在东码头的中继器里发现了刻有____字样和七个名字的芯片。
death:2.hook: The seventh name on the list was still blank.
death:2.line: '*Death* is the message — someone wants us to stop searching.'

freedom:2.en: The coded graffiti covered the entire tunnel wall, line after line of cipher-text. When I finally decoded it, every sentence meant the same thing: *freedom* is the signal that no one can encrypt. Grey Crow had written it himself, months ago.
freedom:2.cnHint: 隧道墙上灰鸦留下的密文全部指向同一个词——____。
freedom:2.hook: Zero's footsteps echoed at the tunnel entrance behind me.
freedom:2.line: '*Freedom* is the only broadcast Zero cannot jam.'

thinking:1.en: Rain hammered the street outside Zero's last known drop point. I pressed my back against the cold wall, running every angle through my head. Grey Crow had warned me: act too fast and the whole net collapses. My *thinking* was simple — wait, watch, and let Zero make the first move.
thinking:1.cnHint: 我在雨中等待，用____判断该何时出手。
thinking:1.hook: Then a shadow crossed the alley, moving too fast to be human.
thinking:1.line: 'My *thinking* is this: we wait until he blinks first.'

cover:1.en: The open market on Fifth Canal was the perfect place to disappear. Vendors shouted over each other, neon signs bled colour into the puddles, and the crowd was thick and loud. Ali pulled her hood low. 'We need *cover*,' she said, stepping between two stalls selling black-market signal chips.
cover:1.cnHint: 阿栗在喧闹的市场里寻求____，以躲避追踪者的视线。
cover:1.hook: Behind us, a scanner drone dropped below the rooftop line.
cover:1.line: 'We need *cover* right now — that drone is already scanning faces.'

recommendation:1.en: Grey Crow met me under the broken overpass at dawn, his coat soaked through. He slid a data chip across the wet concrete without a word. On it was a single *recommendation*: avoid the eastern checkpoint at all costs, because Zero had already bought the guards there.
recommendation:1.cnHint: 灰鸦给了我一条关键的____，警告我绕开某个危险地点。
recommendation:1.hook: I pocketed the chip and heard boots echo behind me.
recommendation:1.line: 'My *recommendation* — do not walk through that gate tonight.'

identity:1.en: The street ID scanner at the bridge entrance flickered green for the man ahead of me, then red for me. I handed the guard a forged card Ali had printed two hours ago. My real *identity* was buried under seven layers of false data — but the scanner hummed and paused, reading deeper.
identity:1.cnHint: 我用假证件掩盖真实的____，却发现扫描仪开始深度检测。
identity:1.hook: The guard's hand moved slowly toward the alarm panel.
identity:1.line: 'Your *identity* does not match any registered citizen — step aside.'

conventional:1.en: Zero never used *conventional* methods. While every other operator in Harbor City relied on encrypted text drops, he spoke his orders aloud in crowded places, trusting noise to swallow the words. I stood three steps behind him at the outdoor tram stop, straining to catch every syllable above the rain.
conventional:1.cnHint: 零点不使用____的传递方式，让我很难追踪他的指令。
conventional:1.hook: He turned his head slightly, as if he already knew I was there.
conventional:1.line: 'Nothing *conventional* — that is exactly why they never catch me.'

agent:1.en: The contact Grey Crow had named was waiting by the canal gate, collar up against the wind. She introduced herself as the last active *agent* inside Zero's outer ring — someone who had spent three years feeding small lies upward to protect the bigger truth hidden underneath.
agent:1.cnHint: 一位长期潜伏的____在运河边等着与我接头。
agent:1.hook: She glanced left, then said, 'We have about ninety seconds.'
agent:1.line: 'I am the only *agent* left who knows where the files are buried.'

cash:1.en: The night vendor at the corner refused to touch any digital payment. 'Only *cash*,' he said, eyes moving to the camera cluster above us. Ali counted out the worn notes while I watched the far end of the street, where a black car had been idling for the last four minutes.
cash:1.cnHint: 街角的商贩只收____，让我们暴露了行踪的时间。
cash:1.hook: The black car's door opened, and no one got out.
cash:1.line: 'No chips, no scan — *cash* only, or I shut the window right now.'

competition:1.en: Grey Crow told me Zero had entered the black-channel *competition* — a silent auction where operators bid for control of Harbor City's main signal tower. Whoever won could rewrite every broadcast in the city. I stood at the edge of the plaza, watching bidders arrive in ones and twos, faces hidden.
competition:1.cnHint: 零点参加了一场争夺信号塔控制权的____，我混入现场监视。
competition:1.hook: Ali's voice crackled in my ear: 'Grey Crow just went dark.'
competition:1.line: 'This *competition* has only one prize — and only one of us leaves.'

overall:2.en: Grey Crow spread the stolen city map across the wet floor of the drainage tunnel. Red markers covered every block. 'The *overall* picture is worse than I feared,' he said. Every sector of Harbor City had been compromised. Zero had not struck one target — he had struck all of them.
overall:2.cnHint: 灰鸦在排水隧道里展开城市地图，发现____情况比想象中糟糕得多。
overall:2.hook: One sector had no red mark — and that silence was the real threat.
overall:2.line: 'The *overall* picture is worse than I feared.'

resident:2.en: The old arcade on Tide Street was dark. Every *resident* of the block had vanished overnight — no bags packed, no notes left. Ali knelt beside an empty chair and found a single warm cup of tea. Someone had been here minutes ago. Whoever cleared this street worked fast and knew every face.
resident:2.cnHint: 阿栗发现街区的____们已经神秘消失，只留下一杯还温热的茶。
resident:2.hook: The tea was still steaming — they had just missed someone.
resident:2.line: 'Every *resident* on this block is gone — not one stayed behind.'

willing:2.en: I found the informant behind the broken vending machine on Level B3. He stared at the floor. I asked him to name Zero's contact. He shook his head once. 'I am not *willing* to die for your case,' he whispered. Then the lights cut out, and when they came back, he was gone.
willing:2.cnHint: 线人拒绝提供情报，说自己不____为我的任务冒死，随后神秘消失。
willing:2.hook: His empty chair still rocked — someone had pulled him out fast.
willing:2.line: 'I am not *willing* to die for your case.'

failure:2.en: Ali handed me the cracked data chip. The signal trace had collapsed mid-run. '*Failure* to decode it now means Zero moves tonight,' she said, her voice flat and steady. She was already at the backup terminal, fingers moving. I watched the progress bar crawl. Outside, thunder rolled over Harbor City's wet rooftops.
failure:2.cnHint: 解码芯片失败意味着零点今晚就会行动，阿栗正在争分夺秒地尝试备用终端。
failure:2.hook: The progress bar froze at ninety-nine percent and did not move.
failure:2.line: '*Failure* to decode it now means Zero moves tonight.'

dog:2.en: A small *dog* sat perfectly still in the center of the flooded underpass, staring at the north wall. No owner. No collar. Just a blinking red light clipped to its back. Grey Crow grabbed my arm. 'That animal is a relay node,' he breathed. 'Zero is listening to us right now.'
dog:2.cnHint: 一只陌生的____安静地坐在地下通道，身上夹着红色信号灯，可能是零点的监听装置。
dog:2.hook: The red light blinked once, then went dark — transmission complete.
dog:2.line: 'That *dog* is not lost — it is Zero's ears on the ground.'

busy:2.en: The sky market above Pier 9 was *busy* even at midnight — noodle carts, loud music, shoulder-to-shoulder crowds. Perfect cover. Ali had traced the signal drop to a stall in the middle of the noise. We pushed through the crowd. By the time we reached the stall, the vendor's seat was empty and cold.
busy:2.cnHint: 午夜的天空市场依然____，阿栗追踪到的信号源就藏在人群中的一个摊位里。
busy:2.hook: Under the empty seat was a folded note addressed to me by name.
busy:2.line: 'Stay close — a *busy* crowd is Zero's favourite hiding place.'

lie:2.en: The archive room was sealed. Grey Crow pointed to the floor: a thin line of light where no window existed. 'The real door must *lie* behind that shelf,' he said. We moved the shelf. Behind it was not a door — it was a staircase going down, and from below came the faint sound of a broadcast we were never meant to hear.
lie:2.cnHint: 灰鸦认为真正的入口____在书架后面，移开后发现的却是一段通往地下的楼梯。
lie:2.hook: The broadcast below spoke one word, over and over: my name.
lie:2.line: 'The answer must *lie* behind what everyone has been told to ignore.'

north:2.en: The signal pointed *north* — past the wall, past the dead relay towers, into the grey belt of Harbor City that no map named anymore. Ali checked her scanner twice. Grey Crow said nothing, only turned up his collar against the rain. That direction was Zero's last known position. It was also, I now remembered, where I had grown up.
north:2.cnHint: 信号指向____方，那是Harbor City没有地图标注的灰色地带，也是零点最后出现的地方。
north:2.hook: I had not been north of the wall since the night my partner disappeared.
north:2.line: 'The signal goes *north* — into the part of the city that was erased.'
